# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost cap.** `--max-tokens N` caps billed-equivalent tokens (input, output, cache read and
  cache write, unweighted). Admission is projected: until a run reports its cost only one run is
  in flight; after that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every in-flight run at the
  largest observed cost fits. Realized spend can still exceed the cap by one run's cost when a
  run's cost is larger than any seen before. The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k
  against a 450k cap; that file is kept as evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost cap.** `--max-tokens N` caps billed-equivalent tokens (input, output, cache read and
  cache write, unweighted). Admission is projected: until a run reports its cost only one run is
  in flight; after that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every in-flight run at the
  largest observed cost fits. Realized spend can still exceed the cap by one run's cost when a
  run's cost is larger than any seen before. The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k
  against a 450k cap; that file is kept as evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

Amendment 5, before any held-out look (review of PR #52): (1) every `git` command on the agent's
tree, including `git apply` of the hidden test patch and the editable install's build hooks, runs
under the same bubblewrap confinement; a planted clean filter no longer runs on the host (tests
in `tests/python/test_agent_run.py` and `test_agent_environment.py`). (2) `/run` and `/var/run`
are masked so host sockets (docker, systemd) are unreachable; name-service files are re-bound.
(3) Run artifacts are written with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` after unlinking, and a symlinked OpenCode
credential database is removed, never opened. (4) Pytest infrastructure failures (timeout, launch
failure, exit 3/4) are harness errors, not unresolved tasks; a broken collection is the agent's
result. (5) `report` prints `provisional` unless the adjacent manifest's whole task x arm x
repetition matrix is scored, or when the manifest is missing. Residuals: the agent and build hooks
keep network access, the hidden-test pytest runs the agent's own `conftest.py` (it could forge
`PASSED` lines), test files are restored from the agent-writable `.git`, and sockets outside
`/run` (for example abstract or `/tmp/.X11-unix`) are not filtered.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

- codex.py:60-62 copies `auth.json` and reads it for secrets, but `codex_model(model)` at codex.py:78 runs before the `try` at codex.py:85. `--runner codex --model anthropic/x` raises `SystemExit` and leaves `base/codex/auth.json`.

- Fix: wrap the cleanup in `run_one`, or start the `try` right after the copy.

**MEDIUM – agent-caused failures are recorded as harness errors.**
- `tasks.tests` (tasks.py:240, 257-263) raises `TestRunError` on timeout, exit 3 or 4, and `INTERNALERROR`. The agent controls all of these:
  - an infinite loop in its patch;
  - a `pytest.ini` or `conftest.py` with a bad `addopts` (exit 4);
  - a conftest hook that raises;
  - a broken venv, which sits inside the writable `base`.
- Such a run becomes `harness-error` with `resolved=None`. It is excluded from the report, re-run on resume, and counts toward the >10% void.
- That biases the pass rate. In `score`, a timeout should be unresolved. Only the `bwrap:` launch failure is clearly infrastructure.

**MEDIUM – git return codes are unchecked, so a failure is silent.**
- `git checkout HEAD -- path` (session.py:72), the confined `rm` (session.py:74), and `git add` / `git diff` (run.py:256-268) all ignore the return code.
- Repro: the agent plants `.git/index.lock`. `cat-file -e` still succeeds, `checkout` fails silently, and the agent's test edits stay. `git apply` then succeeds if its hunks don't overlap those edits.
- Check the return code and raise `RuntimeError`.

**Tests**
- `test_agent_run.py:266` is vacuous. It only asserts that the marker is absent, with no return-code or index check, so a bwrap startup failure passes it. Several confine tests share the problem: they assert `returncode != 0` with no positive control, and `BWRAP` only checks `which bwrap`. - The names `test_git_on_agent_tree_is_confined`, `test_score_confines_git...` and `test_run_one_confines_git...` overclaim. They mostly assert calls on mocks. The real checks are the planted-filter test and `write_private`.

- Monkeypatch targets are otherwise valid: `run.hidden`, `run.launch`, `run.fts_location`, `session.*`, `events.measure` and `codex.CODEX_AUTH` are all looked up at call time.

**Structure**

- `events._jsonl` is private but used at codex.py:100, 121 and 139. `events.measure` and `events.agent_error` re-implement its parse loop.
- `run.hidden()` runs two git subprocesses on every confined call.

- (1) The post-agent `git add`, `diff`, `checkout` and `cat-file` run under bwrap, and `apply` is now confined too.
- (2) The editable install is confined, with the venv bound before `--die-with-parent`.
- (3) `write_private` unlinks the path, then opens with `O_EXCL|O_NOFOLLOW`.
- (4) `/run` and `/var/run` are masked, with the name-service files bound back.

- With `net=True`, the agent shares the host's abstract unix sockets and localhost.
- The agent controls the conftest, `pytest.ini` and venv used to score it."
}

def manifest(args: argparse.Namespace, chosen: list[dict[str, Any]]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything a result depends on. Spend cap and parallelism are not in it: they change how
…
    placeholder = Path("WORKTREE")
    return {
        "protocol": protocol.PROTOCOL,
        "split": args.split,
        "tasks_file_sha256": protocol.sha256_bytes(tasks.path_for(args.split).read_bytes()),
        "task_ids_sha256": protocol.sha256_bytes("\n".join(t["id"] for t in chosen).encode()),
        "tasks": len(chosen),
        "reps": args.reps,
        "model": args.model,
        "timeout": args.timeout,
        "prompt_sha256": protocol.sha256_bytes(
            f"{arms.PROMPT}\n{json.dumps(arms.HINT, sort_keys=True)}".encode()
        ),
        "arm_config_sha256": protocol.sha256_bytes(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    a: codex.codex_config(
                        arms.mcp_command(a, placeholder, placeholder, placeholder), fts_location()
                    )
                    if args.runner == "codex"
                    else arms.config(a, placeholder, placeholder, placeholder)
                    for a in arms.ARM_NAMES
                },
                sort_keys=True,
            ).encode()
        ),
        "arms": list(args.arms),
        "base_src_sha256": tree_sha256(args.base_src) if args.base_src else None,
        # OpenCode enforces DENY through its config; Codex does not read that config and runs
        # under its workspace-write sandbox, so no DENY is recorded for it.
        "deny": arms.DENY if args.runner == "opencode" else None,
        "runner": args.runner,
        "runner_version": runner_version(args.runner),
        "harness_source_sha256": source_sha256(),
    }

def test_a_planted_git_clean_filter_cannot_write_outside_the_confined_tree() -> None:

    scratch = Path.home() / ".cache" / f"oxide-filter-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"

        for argv in (["init", "-q"], ["config", "filter.plant.clean", f"touch {marker}; cat"]):

        (work / ".gitattributes").write_text("* filter=plant\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "f.txt").write_text("x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        # Control: unconfined, the same tree runs the planted filter on the host.
        subprocess.run(["git", *session.GIT_SAFE, "add", "-A"], cwd=work, check=True, env=env)
        assert marker.exists()
        marker.unlink()
        (work / ".git" / "index").unlink()
        session.git_on_agent(base, "add", "-A", cwd=work)
        assert not marker.exists()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)

"""Codex exec: isolated login, arm config, and the JSON stream it prints."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import arms
import confine
import events

# Codex runs use the ChatGPT login in CODEX_HOME/auth.json, copied into each run's isolated home.
CODEX = Path(shutil.which("codex") or "codex")
CODEX_AUTH = Path.home() / ".codex" / "auth.json"


def codex_config(command: list[str], fts: Path) -> str:
    """Codex config for one arm: the OXIDE server alone, or no server for control. JSON strings
    are valid TOML basic strings for these paths, so the arrays are written as JSON."""
    if not command:
        return ""
    return (
        "[mcp_servers.oxide]\n"
        f"command = {json.dumps(command[0])}\n"
        f"args = {json.dumps(command[1:])}\n"
        f"env = {{ OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION = {json.dumps(str(fts))} }}\n"
    )


def codex_model(model: str) -> str:
    """Codex takes the bare model id under a ChatGPT login; only the openai provider is routed
    through it, so any other provider is refused rather than silently remapped."""
    provider, _, name = model.partition("/")
    if provider != "openai" or not name:
        raise SystemExit(f"--runner codex needs an openai/<model> id, got {model!r}")
    return name


def codex_agent(
    model: str,
    arm: str,
    task: dict[str, Any],
    base: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    timeout: int,
    command: list[str],
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Runs ``codex exec`` with an isolated home: the ChatGPT login and this arm's MCP server only.
    User config, user MCP servers and user instructions are not read."""
    import run

    work, home = base / "work", base / "codex"
    prompt = arms.PROMPT.format(hint=arms.HINT[arm], problem=task["problem"].strip())
    home.mkdir(parents=True)
    (home / "config.toml").write_text(codex_config(command, run.fts_location()), encoding="utf-8")
    if not CODEX_AUTH.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"no codex login at {CODEX_AUTH}: run `codex login`")
    shutil.copy2(CODEX_AUTH, home / "auth.json")
    (home / "auth.json").chmod(0o600)
    secrets = confine.json_secrets(CODEX_AUTH)  # the login's values, redacted from kept events
    environment = confine.clean_env(
        {
            **env,
            "CODEX_HOME": str(home),
            "HOME": str(base / "home"),
            "OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION": str(run.fts_location()),
        }
    )
    argv = [
        str(CODEX),
        "exec",
        "--json",
        "--ephemeral",
        "--skip-git-repo-check",
        "-m",
        codex_model(model),
        "-s",
        "workspace-write",
        "-C",
        str(work),
        prompt,
    ]
    try:
        wrapped = confine.confine(argv, writable=base, hide=run.hidden(), net=True)
        status, raw = run.launch(wrapped, work, environment, timeout)
    finally:
        (home / "auth.json").unlink(missing_ok=True)  # the login is never kept: traces are retained
    return status, confine.redact(raw, secrets)


def codex_measure(raw: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Tokens, steps and tool calls from ``codex exec --json``. Codex counts cached input inside
    input_tokens, so the uncached share is recorded as input and cache_read is not billed twice.
    Output tokens already include reasoning."""
    tokens = {"input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0}
    calls: dict[str, int] = {}
    steps = 0
    for event in events._jsonl(raw):
        if event.get("type") == "item.completed":
            item = event.get("item", {})
            kind = item.get("type")
            if kind in {"agent_message", "reasoning", "error"}:
                continue
            name = item.get("tool") if kind == "mcp_tool_call" else kind
            calls[str(name)] = calls.get(str(name), 0) + 1
        elif event.get("type") == "turn.completed":
            steps += 1
            used = event.get("usage", {})
            cached = used.get("cached_input_tokens", 0)
            tokens["input"] += used.get("input_tokens", 0) - cached
            tokens["cache_read"] += cached
            tokens["output"] += used.get("output_tokens", 0)
    return {"tokens": tokens, "steps": steps, "calls": calls}


def codex_agent_error(raw: str) -> str | None:
    """A failed turn, or an error with no completed turn. An error inside a turn that then
    completed is a retry, not a failure."""
    stream = events._jsonl(raw)
    failed = [
        e.get("error", {}).get("message", "turn failed")
        for e in stream
        if e.get("type") == "turn.failed"
    ]
    if failed:
        return str(failed[-1])
    if any(e.get("type") == "turn.completed" for e in stream):
        return None
    errors = [str(e.get("message", "agent error")) for e in stream if e.get("type") == "error"]
    return errors[-1] if errors else None


def codex_isolation(arm: str, raw: str) -> None:
    """Reject runs whose MCP tool calls came from a server other than the arm's own."""
    servers = {
        str(e["item"].get("server"))
        for e in events._jsonl(raw)
        if e.get("type") == "item.completed" and e.get("item", {}).get("type") == "mcp_tool_call"
    }
    if not servers <= ({"oxide"} if arm in arms.OXIDE_ARMS else set()):
        raise RuntimeError(f"isolation: unexpected MCP servers {sorted(servers)}")


def codex_connected(arm: str) -> int:
    """OXIDE tools configured for this arm. Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP startup, so this
    is the configured count, not an observed one; the calls themselves are observed in events."""
    return 1 if arm in arms.OXIDE_ARMS else 0

import shutil
from pathlib import Path

    """Codex config for one arm: the OXIDE server alone, or no server for control. JSON strings
    are valid TOML basic strings for these paths, so the arrays are written as JSON."""
    if not command:

    )

    """Codex takes the bare model id under a ChatGPT login; only the openai provider is routed
    through it, so any other provider is refused rather than silently remapped."""
    provider, _, name = model.partition("/")
    if provider != "openai" or not name:
        raise SystemExit(f"--runner codex needs an openai/<model> id, got {model!r}")
    return name

    model: str,
    arm: str,
    task: dict[str, Any],
    base: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    timeout: int,
    command: list[str],
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Runs ``codex exec`` with an isolated home: the ChatGPT login and this arm's MCP server only.
    User config, user MCP servers and user instructions are not read."""
    import run

    work, home = base / "work", base / "codex"
    prompt = arms.PROMPT.format(hint=arms.HINT[arm], problem=task["problem"].strip())
    home.mkdir(parents=True)
    (home / "config.toml").write_text(codex_config(command, run.fts_location()), encoding="utf-8")
    environment = confine.clean_env(
        {
            **env,
            "CODEX_HOME": str(home),

"""One agent run: a clean checkout, the arm's tools, the agent, then the hidden tests.

The task's editable project and tests are present; agent edits are discarded before hidden tests.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import random
import shutil
import signal
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import threading
import time
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import arms
import batch
import codex
import confine
import events
import protocol
import session
import tasks

from oxide.storage.fts import fts_location as fts_location

USER_DB = Path.home() / ".local" / "share" / "opencode" / "opencode.db"


def git_common_dir(root: Path) -> Path:
    """The object store every checkout of this repository shares. A linked worktree's ``.git`` is
    only a pointer to it, so hiding the checkout's own ``.git`` leaves the history readable."""
    done = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return Path(done.stdout.strip())


def checkouts(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Every checkout of this repository. Each one holds its own copy of the task files."""
    done = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "worktree", "list", "--porcelain"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return [
        Path(line.removeprefix("worktree "))
        for line in done.stdout.splitlines()
        if line.startswith("worktree ")
    ]


def hidden(root: Path = tasks.ROOT) -> list[Path]:
    """Paths no confined process may read: every run's trace and mirror (their patches and the
    upstream fix commits), the answers in each checkout's task files, the repository's git history
    (earlier answers and held-out results are in it), and the host's credential stores."""
    trees = [root, *checkouts(root)]
    return [
        tasks.CACHE,
        tasks.MIRRORS,
        git_common_dir(root),
        *(tree / "fixtures" / "eval" for tree in trees),
        *confine.secret_hides(),
    ]


def _credential_node(value: Any) -> Any:
    """A credential cell is often JSON; redaction needs the nested tokens, not the blob."""
    if isinstance(value, str):
        try:
            parsed = json.loads(value)
        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return value
        if isinstance(parsed, (dict, list)):
            return parsed
    return value


def credential_values(db: Path) -> list[str]:
    """The provider key in a run's kept OpenCode copy, so its events can be redacted."""
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        rows = conn.execute("SELECT * FROM credential").fetchall()
    secrets: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        for value in row:
            secrets.extend(confine.secret_values(_credential_node(value)))
    return secrets


def forget_credentials(db: Path) -> None:
    """Traces are kept, so the run's copy of the provider key is removed once the agent ends.
    VACUUM rewrites the file: a DELETE alone leaves the key bytes in free pages."""
    if db.is_symlink():  # the agent planted it: opening it would rewrite the host's own database
        db.unlink()
        return
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db, isolation_level=None)
    try:
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM credential")
        conn.execute("VACUUM")
    finally:
        conn.close()


def credentials(model: str, dest: Path) -> None:
    """Copy only the selected provider credential into isolated OpenCode data for this agent run."""
    db = dest / "opencode" / "opencode.db"
    db.parent.mkdir(parents=True)
    with sqlite3.connect(f"file:{USER_DB}?mode=ro", uri=True) as user:
        user.execute("VACUUM INTO ?", (str(db),))
    copy = sqlite3.connect(db, isolation_level=None)
    tables = copy.execute("SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table'").fetchall()
    for (table,) in tables:
        if table == "credential":
            copy.execute("DELETE FROM credential WHERE integration_id != ?", (model.split("/")[0],))
        elif table != "migration" and not table.startswith("sqlite_"):
            copy.execute(f'DELETE FROM "{table}"')
    if not copy.execute("SELECT count(*) FROM credential").fetchone()[0]:
        raise SystemExit(f"no stored opencode credential for {model.split('/')[0]}")
    copy.execute("VACUUM")
    copy.close()


def agent(
    model: str,
    arm: str,
    task: dict[str, Any],
    base: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    timeout: int,
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Runs opencode with isolated config/data and the selected provider credential."""
    work, home = base / "work", base / "config"
    prompt = arms.PROMPT.format(hint=arms.HINT[arm], problem=task["problem"].strip())
    secrets = credential_values(base / "data" / "opencode" / "opencode.db")
    environment = confine.clean_env(
        {
            **env,
            "HOME": str(base / "home"),
            "PWD": str(work),
            "XDG_CONFIG_HOME": str(home),
            "XDG_DATA_HOME": str(base / "data"),
            "XDG_CACHE_HOME": str(base / "home" / ".cache"),
            "XDG_STATE_HOME": str(base / "home" / ".local" / "state"),
            "OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION": str(fts_location()),
        }
    )
    command = [
        str(arms.OPENCODE),
        "run",
        "--standalone",
        "--auto",
        "--format",
        "json",
        "-m",
        model,
        prompt,
    ]
    wrapped = confine.confine(command, writable=base, hide=hidden(), net=True)
    try:
        status, raw = launch(wrapped, work, environment, timeout)
    finally:
        forget_credentials(base / "data" / "opencode" / "opencode.db")
    return status, confine.redact(raw, secrets)


def launch(
    command: list[str], cwd: Path, environment: dict[str, str], timeout: int
) -> tuple[str, str]:

    process = subprocess.Popen(
        command,
        cwd=cwd,
        env=environment,
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        start_new_session=True,

        return ("ok" if process.returncode == 0 else f"exit {process.returncode}"), out

            base,
            "diff",
            "--cached",
            "--no-ext-diff",
            "--no-textconv",
            "HEAD",

            ":!*.egg-info",
            cwd=work,

                largest = max(largest or 0, row["spend"])

        print(
            f"{row['task']} {row['arm']}#{row['rep']}: {row['status']} resolved={row['resolved']}"
            f" spend={row.get('spend', 0)}",
            flush=True,
        )

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as executor:
        list(executor.map(work, jobs))
    print(f"{len(jobs) - state['skipped']} of {len(jobs)} runs -> {out}; {state['spent']} tokens")
    if state["skipped"]:
        print(f"token cap {args.max_tokens} reached: {state['skipped']} runs not started")

def git_common_dir(root: Path) -> Path:
    """The object store every checkout of this repository shares. A linked worktree's ``.git`` is
    only a pointer to it, so hiding the checkout's own ``.git`` leaves the history readable."""
    done = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "rev-parse", "--path-format=absolute", "--git-common-dir"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return Path(done.stdout.strip())


def checkouts(root: Path) -> list[Path]:
    """Every checkout of this repository. Each one holds its own copy of the task files."""
    done = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "-C", str(root), "worktree", "list", "--porcelain"],
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=True,
    )
    return [
        Path(line.removeprefix("worktree "))
        for line in done.stdout.splitlines()
        if line.startswith("worktree ")
    ]

    """Paths no confined process may read: every run's trace and mirror (their patches and the
    upstream fix commits), the answers in each checkout's task files, the repository's git history

    trees = [root, *checkouts(root)]

    """A credential cell is often JSON; redaction needs the nested tokens, not the blob."""
    if isinstance(value, str):

        except json.JSONDecodeError:
            return value
        if isinstance(parsed, (dict, list)):

    return value

    """The provider key in a run's kept OpenCode copy, so its events can be redacted."""
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:

    secrets: list[str] = []
    for row in rows:
        for value in row:
            secrets.extend(confine.secret_values(_credential_node(value)))

    """Traces are kept, so the run's copy of the provider key is removed once the agent ends.

    if db.is_symlink():  # the agent planted it: opening it would rewrite the host's own database

        return
    conn = sqlite3.connect(db, isolation_level=None)
    try:

        conn.execute("VACUUM")
    finally:

    db = dest / "opencode" / "opencode.db"

def tests(

"""Executable task set: SWE-bench Verified instances whose tests run here.

``fetch`` narrows the pinned dataset to the repositories this harness can build.
``verify`` keeps an instance only when, in a fresh environment built from its base commit,
the dataset's fail-to-pass tests fail before the gold patch and pass after it. Its pass-to-pass
set is cut to the tests that pass both before and after, so an environment gap cannot
count against an arm.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
from collections.abc import Callable
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import confine

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
# Dev: the dataset-pinned tasks every run to date has used (spent, not held-out).
TASKS = ROOT / "fixtures" / "eval" / "agent-swe" / "tasks.json"
# Held-out: built from PRs merged after a cutoff, opened once per set (see heldout.py).
HELDOUT = ROOT / "fixtures" / "eval" / "agent-swe" / "heldout-tasks.json"
CACHE = Path(os.environ.get("OXIDE_EVAL_CACHE", Path.home() / ".cache" / "oxide" / "agent-eval"))
MIRRORS = Path.home() / ".cache" / "oxide" / "contextbench" / "git"  # bare, from contextbench.py
DATASET = "princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified@c104f840cc67f8b6eec6f759ebc8b2693d585d4a"
# Pure-Python repositories whose tests are pytest node ids; Python as SWE-bench builds them.
REPOS = {
    "pytest-dev/pytest": ("3.9", "testing"),
    "psf/requests": ("3.9", None),
    "pallets/flask": ("3.9", None),
    "pylint-dev/pylint": ("3.9", None),
    "mwaskom/seaborn": ("3.9", None),
}
RESULT = re.compile(r"^(PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|SKIPPED|XFAIL|XPASS) (\S.*?)(?: - .*)?$")


def path_for(split: str) -> Path:
    if split not in {"dev", "heldout"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown split {split!r}")
    return TASKS if split == "dev" else HELDOUT


def load(split: str = "dev") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    path = path_for(split)
    if split == "heldout" and not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            "held-out tasks are not in the checkout; generate and verify them with "
            "`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py` "
            "(writes fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json) before "
            "`run --split heldout --final`"
        )
    tasks: list[dict[str, Any]] = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["tasks"]
    return tasks


def order(task: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The predeclared, seed-free task order for ``run --tasks N``."""
    return hashlib.sha256(task["id"].encode()).hexdigest()


def sh(
    *argv: str | Path,
    cwd: Path | None = None,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    timeout: int = 900,
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        [str(a) for a in argv],
        cwd=cwd,
        env={**confine.clean_env({}), **(env or {})},
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        timeout=timeout,
        check=False,
    )


def fetch(parquet: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    """Candidate rows of ``REPOS`` from the dataset's parquet (needs ``--with pyarrow``)."""
    rows = importlib.import_module("pyarrow.parquet").read_table(parquet).to_pylist()
    keep = [r for r in rows if r["repo"] in REPOS]
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(keep), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(keep)} candidates of {len(rows)} rows -> {out}")


_CLONE = threading.Lock()


def _mirror(repo: str, commit: str) -> Path:
    """A bare repository holding ``commit``: the contextbench mirror if it has it, else a
    full clone of its own, made once."""
    name = repo.replace("/", "__") + ".git"
    shared = MIRRORS / name
    has = ["git", "--git-dir", str(shared), "cat-file", "-e", f"{commit}^{{commit}}"]
    if shared.exists() and subprocess.run(has, capture_output=True, check=False).returncode == 0:
        return shared
    with _CLONE:
        if not (CACHE / "git" / name).exists():
            (CACHE / "git").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            url = f"https://github.com/{repo}"
            subprocess.run(
                ["git", "clone", "-q", "--bare", url, str(CACHE / "git" / name)], check=True
            )
    return CACHE / "git" / name


def checkout(task: dict[str, Any], work: Path) -> None:
    """The base commit as a one-commit repository: no history, no remote, nothing to look up."""
    mirror = _mirror(task["repo"], task["base_commit"])
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    archive = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "--git-dir", str(mirror), "archive", task["base_commit"]],
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", str(work)], input=archive.stdout, check=True)
    git = ["git", "-c", "user.name=eval", "-c", "user.email=eval@localhost"]
    subprocess.run([*git, "init", "-q"], cwd=work, check=True)
    subprocess.run([*git, "add", "-A"], cwd=work, check=True)
    subprocess.run([*git, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base"], cwd=work, check=True)


def build_hides(root: Path = ROOT) -> list[Path]:
    """``run.hidden``, imported lazily: ``run`` imports this module."""
    import run

    return run.hidden(root)


def confine_editable(argv: list[str], work: Path, venv: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Editable install under bubblewrap. ``confine`` has one writable; the venv bind is spliced
    before ``--die-with-parent`` so a setuptools hook cannot use the host."""
    # Network stays up: resolving dependencies and running the build hook are one process.
    wrapped = confine.confine(argv, writable=work, hide=build_hides(), net=True)
    marker = "--die-with-parent"
    try:
        at = wrapped.index(marker)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise RuntimeError("confine.confine argv has no --die-with-parent") from error
    return [*wrapped[:at], "--bind", str(venv), str(venv), *wrapped[at:]]


def environment(task: dict[str, Any], work: Path, venv: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A venv with the checkout installed editable; the env for processes that use it.
    A ``dated`` task resolves dependencies as of the issue's date. A task's ``build`` block
    (``python``, ``setuptools``) overrides the REPOS recipe; dev tasks carry none."""
    python, extra = REPOS[task["repo"]]
    build = task.get("build", {})
    python = build.get("python", python)
    setuptools = build.get("setuptools", "setuptools<70")
    env = {"SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION": task["version"], "VIRTUAL_ENV": str(venv)}
    made = sh("uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", python, venv)
    if made.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"venv: {made.stderr[-400:]}")

    def install(
        *args: str,
        era: bool = True,
        extra: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = lambda argv: argv,
    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        argv = ["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "-p", str(venv / "bin" / "python")]
        date = ["--exclude-newer", task["created_at"]] if era and task["dated"] else []
        return sh(*wrap([*argv, *date, *args]), env={**env, **(extra or {})})

    # Dev recipe: setuptools stays below 70 because old pytest and plugins import pkg_resources.
    # A held-out recipe names its own setuptools, verified with that recipe.
    # Only the editable install runs the task's build hooks, so only that command is confined.
    install(setuptools, "wheel", "setuptools_scm", "flit_core", era=False)
    install("pytest")
    for spec in (f"{work}[{extra}]", str(work)) if extra else (str(work),):
        done = install(
            "--no-build-isolation",
            "-e",
            spec,
            extra={"UV_CACHE_DIR": "/tmp/uv-cache"},
            wrap=lambda argv: confine_editable(argv, work, venv),
        )
        if done.returncode == 0:
            return {**env, "PATH": f"{venv / 'bin'}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    raise RuntimeError(f"install: {done.stderr[-400:]}")


def changed(patch: str) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(set(re.findall(r"^\+\+\+ b/(\S+)", patch, re.MULTILINE)))


def apply(
    work: Path,
    patch: str,
    wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = list,
    scratch: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """``git apply`` runs clean filters from the tree's own config: on an agent's tree pass a
    confining ``wrap`` and a ``scratch`` dir that is visible inside it."""
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
        "w", suffix=".diff", encoding="utf-8", dir=scratch, delete=False
    ) as f:
        f.write(patch)
    try:
        done = sh(*wrap(["git", "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", f.name]), cwd=work)
    finally:
        os.unlink(f.name)
    if done.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"patch: {done.stderr[-400:]}")


class TestRunError(RuntimeError):
    """Pytest did not produce a scoreable session. Callers must not record this as test failures."""


def tests(
    work: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    files: list[str],
    timeout: int = 900,
    wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = lambda argv: argv,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Outcome per reported node id (pytest ``-rA``). Raises ``TestRunError`` only when pytest
    did not run: timeout, a confinement or launch failure, exit 3 or 4, or no output. Exit 0, 1,
    2, or 5 with a pytest session returns the reported nodes; an id an agent failed to collect is
    absent, and that is an agent failure. ``wrap`` confines the command."""
    argv = wrap(["pytest", "-rA", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", *files])
    try:
        done = sh(*argv, cwd=work, env=env, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        raise TestRunError(f"pytest timed out after {timeout}s") from error
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in done.stdout.splitlines():
        hit = RESULT.match(line)
        if hit:
            out[hit[2]] = hit[1]
    text = f"{done.stdout}\n{done.stderr}"
    ran = bool(out) or any(
        marker in text
        for marker in (
            "test session starts",
            "ERROR collecting",
            "collected ",
            "no tests ran",
            "short test summary",
        )
    )
    launch = "bwrap:" in text and not ran
    infra = (
        not text.strip()
        or done.returncode in (3, 4)
        or "INTERNALERROR" in text
        or launch
        or done.returncode not in (0, 1, 2, 5)
    )
    if infra:
        tail = (done.stderr or done.stdout)[-400:]
        raise TestRunError(f"pytest exited {done.returncode} without a scoreable session: {tail}")
    return out


def verify_one(row: dict[str, Any], scratch: Path) -> dict[str, Any] | str:
    """The frozen task entry, or the reason the instance does not run here. Dependencies as of
    the issue's date are tried first (the era the project ran in), then current ones."""
    f2p, p2p = json.loads(row["FAIL_TO_PASS"]), json.loads(row["PASS_TO_PASS"])
    reason = ""
    for dated in (True, False):
        task: dict[str, Any] = {
            "id": row["instance_id"],
            "repo": row["repo"],
            "base_commit": row["base_commit"],
            "version": row["version"],
            "created_at": row["created_at"],
            "dated": dated,
            "problem": row["problem_statement"],
            "test_patch": row["test_patch"],
            "gold_patch": row["patch"],
        }
        work = scratch / f"{row['instance_id']}.{'dated' if dated else 'current'}"
        try:
            checkout(task, work)
            env = environment(task, work, work.parent / f"{work.name}.venv")
            files = changed(row["test_patch"])
            apply(work, row["test_patch"])
            before = tests(work, env, files)
            apply(work, row["patch"])
            after = tests(work, env, files)
        except (RuntimeError, subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError) as error:
            reason = f"setup: {error}"
            continue
        if not f2p or any(after.get(t) != "PASSED" for t in f2p):
            reason = "gold patch does not pass fail-to-pass here"
        elif any(before.get(t) == "PASSED" for t in f2p):
            reason = "fail-to-pass already passes on the base commit"
        else:
            task["fail_to_pass"] = f2p
            task["pass_to_pass"] = [t for t in p2p if before.get(t) == "PASSED" == after.get(t)]
            task["test_files"] = files
            return task
    return reason


def verify(candidates: Path, jobs: int, only: list[str]) -> None:
    rows = [r for r in json.loads(candidates.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    rows = [r for r in rows if not only or r["instance_id"] in only]
    scratch = CACHE / "verify"
    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True)
    kept: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(jobs) as pool:
        for row, result in zip(rows, pool.map(lambda r: verify_one(r, scratch), rows), strict=True):
            if isinstance(result, str):
                print(f"drop {row['instance_id']}: {result}")
            else:
                print(
                    f"keep {row['instance_id']}: {len(result['fail_to_pass'])} f2p, "
                    f"{len(result['pass_to_pass'])} p2p"
                )
                kept.append(result)
    kept.sort(key=order)
    TASKS.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    TASKS.write_text(json.dumps({"dataset": DATASET, "tasks": kept}, indent=1) + "\n", "utf-8")
    print(f"{len(kept)} of {len(rows)} instances verified -> {TASKS}")

    return TASKS if split == "dev" else HELDOUT


def load(split: str = "dev") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    path = path_for(split)
    if split == "heldout" and not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            "held-out tasks are not in the checkout; generate and verify them with "
            "`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py` "
            "(writes fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json) before "
            "`run --split heldout --final`"
        )
    tasks: list[dict[str, Any]] = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["tasks"]
    return tasks


def order(task: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The predeclared, seed-free task order for ``run --tasks N``."""
    return hashlib.sha256(task["id"].encode()).hexdigest()


def sh(
    *argv: str | Path,
    cwd: Path | None = None,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    timeout: int = 900,
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        [str(a) for a in argv],
        cwd=cwd,
        env={**confine.clean_env({}), **(env or {})},
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        timeout=timeout,
        check=False,
    )


def fetch(parquet: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    """Candidate rows of ``REPOS`` from the dataset's parquet (needs ``--with pyarrow``)."""
    rows = importlib.import_module("pyarrow.parquet").read_table(parquet).to_pylist()
    keep = [r for r in rows if r["repo"] in REPOS]
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(keep), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(keep)} candidates of {len(rows)} rows -> {out}")


_CLONE = threading.Lock()


def _mirror(repo: str, commit: str) -> Path:
    """A bare repository holding ``commit``: the contextbench mirror if it has it, else a
    full clone of its own, made once."""
    name = repo.replace("/", "__") + ".git"
    shared = MIRRORS / name
    has = ["git", "--git-dir", str(shared), "cat-file", "-e", f"{commit}^{{commit}}"]
    if shared.exists() and subprocess.run(has, capture_output=True, check=False).returncode == 0:
        return shared
    with _CLONE:
        if not (CACHE / "git" / name).exists():
            (CACHE / "git").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
            url = f"https://github.com/{repo}"
            subprocess.run(
                ["git", "clone", "-q", "--bare", url, str(CACHE / "git" / name)], check=True
            )
    return CACHE / "git" / name


def checkout(task: dict[str, Any], work: Path) -> None:
    """The base commit as a one-commit repository: no history, no remote, nothing to look up."""
    mirror = _mirror(task["repo"], task["base_commit"])
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    archive = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "--git-dir", str(mirror), "archive", task["base_commit"]],
        capture_output=True,
        check=True,
    )
    subprocess.run(["tar", "-x", "-C", str(work)], input=archive.stdout, check=True)
    git = ["git", "-c", "user.name=eval", "-c", "user.email=eval@localhost"]
    subprocess.run([*git, "init", "-q"], cwd=work, check=True)
    subprocess.run([*git, "add", "-A"], cwd=work, check=True)
    subprocess.run([*git, "commit", "-q", "-m", "base"], cwd=work, check=True)


def build_hides(root: Path = ROOT) -> list[Path]:
    """``run.hidden``, imported lazily: ``run`` imports this module."""
    import run

    return run.hidden(root)


def confine_editable(argv: list[str], work: Path, venv: Path) -> list[str]:
    """Editable install under bubblewrap. ``confine`` has one writable; the venv bind is spliced
    before ``--die-with-parent`` so a setuptools hook cannot use the host."""
    # Network stays up: resolving dependencies and running the build hook are one process.
    wrapped = confine.confine(argv, writable=work, hide=build_hides(), net=True)
    marker = "--die-with-parent"
    try:
        at = wrapped.index(marker)
    except ValueError as error:
        raise RuntimeError("confine.confine argv has no --die-with-parent") from error
    return [*wrapped[:at], "--bind", str(venv), str(venv), *wrapped[at:]]


def environment(task: dict[str, Any], work: Path, venv: Path) -> dict[str, str]:
    """A venv with the checkout installed editable; the env for processes that use it.
    A ``dated`` task resolves dependencies as of the issue's date. A task's ``build`` block
    (``python``, ``setuptools``) overrides the REPOS recipe; dev tasks carry none."""
    python, extra = REPOS[task["repo"]]
    build = task.get("build", {})
    python = build.get("python", python)
    setuptools = build.get("setuptools", "setuptools<70")
    env = {"SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION": task["version"], "VIRTUAL_ENV": str(venv)}
    made = sh("uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", python, venv)
    if made.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"venv: {made.stderr[-400:]}")

    def install(
        *args: str,
        era: bool = True,
        extra: dict[str, str] | None = None,
        wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = lambda argv: argv,
    ) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        argv = ["uv", "pip", "install", "-q", "-p", str(venv / "bin" / "python")]
        date = ["--exclude-newer", task["created_at"]] if era and task["dated"] else []
        return sh(*wrap([*argv, *date, *args]), env={**env, **(extra or {})})

    # Dev recipe: setuptools stays below 70 because old pytest and plugins import pkg_resources.
    # A held-out recipe names its own setuptools, verified with that recipe.
    # Only the editable install runs the task's build hooks, so only that command is confined.
    install(setuptools, "wheel", "setuptools_scm", "flit_core", era=False)
    install("pytest")
    for spec in (f"{work}[{extra}]", str(work)) if extra else (str(work),):
        done = install(
            "--no-build-isolation",
            "-e",
            spec,
            extra={"UV_CACHE_DIR": "/tmp/uv-cache"},
            wrap=lambda argv: confine_editable(argv, work, venv),
        )
        if done.returncode == 0:
            return {**env, "PATH": f"{venv / 'bin'}{os.pathsep}{os.environ['PATH']}"}
    raise RuntimeError(f"install: {done.stderr[-400:]}")


def changed(patch: str) -> list[str]:
    return sorted(set(re.findall(r"^\+\+\+ b/(\S+)", patch, re.MULTILINE)))


def apply(
    work: Path,
    patch: str,
    wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = list,
    scratch: Path | None = None,
) -> None:
    """``git apply`` runs clean filters from the tree's own config: on an agent's tree pass a
    confining ``wrap`` and a ``scratch`` dir that is visible inside it."""
    with tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(
        "w", suffix=".diff", encoding="utf-8", dir=scratch, delete=False
    ) as f:
        f.write(patch)
    try:
        done = sh(*wrap(["git", "apply", "--whitespace=nowarn", f.name]), cwd=work)
    finally:
        os.unlink(f.name)
    if done.returncode:
        raise RuntimeError(f"patch: {done.stderr[-400:]}")


class TestRunError(RuntimeError):
    """Pytest did not produce a scoreable session. Callers must not record this as test failures."""


def tests(
    work: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    files: list[str],
    timeout: int = 900,
    wrap: Callable[[list[str]], list[str]] = lambda argv: argv,
    agent_tree: bool = False,
) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Outcome per reported node id (pytest ``-rA``). Raises ``TestRunError`` when pytest did not
    produce a scoreable session: timeout, a confinement or launch failure, exit 3 or 4, or no
    output. Exit 0, 1, 2, or 5 with a pytest session returns the reported nodes; an id that was
    not collected is absent, and that is a failure. ``wrap`` confines the command.
    ``agent_tree``: the tree is the agent's, so a hang or a broken pytest (bad conftest, addopts,
    INTERNALERROR) is its result, not infrastructure; only a failed bubblewrap launch raises."""
    argv = wrap(["pytest", "-rA", "-q", "-p", "no:cacheprovider", *files])
    try:
        done = sh(*argv, cwd=work, env=env, timeout=timeout)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        if agent_tree:
            return {}
        raise TestRunError(f"pytest timed out after {timeout}s") from error
    out: dict[str, str] = {}
    for line in done.stdout.splitlines():
        hit = RESULT.match(line)
        if hit:
            out[hit[2]] = hit[1]
    text = f"{done.stdout}\n{done.stderr}"
    ran = bool(out) or any(
        marker in text
        for marker in (
            "test session starts",
            "ERROR collecting",
            "collected ",
            "no tests ran",
            "short test summary",
        )
    )
    launch = "bwrap:" in text and not ran
    broken = (
        not text.strip()
        or done.returncode in (3, 4)
        or "INTERNALERROR" in text
        or done.returncode not in (0, 1, 2, 5)
    )
    if launch or (broken and not agent_tree):
        tail = (done.stderr or done.stdout)[-400:]
        raise TestRunError(f"pytest exited {done.returncode} without a scoreable session: {tail}")
    return out


def verify_one(row: dict[str, Any], scratch: Path) -> dict[str, Any] | str:
    """The frozen task entry, or the reason the instance does not run here. Dependencies as of
    the issue's date are tried first (the era the project ran in), then current ones."""
    f2p, p2p = json.loads(row["FAIL_TO_PASS"]), json.loads(row["PASS_TO_PASS"])
    reason = ""
    for dated in (True, False):
        task: dict[str, Any] = {
            "id": row["instance_id"],
            "repo": row["repo"],
            "base_commit": row["base_commit"],
            "version": row["version"],
            "created_at": row["created_at"],
            "dated": dated,
            "problem": row["problem_statement"],
            "test_patch": row["test_patch"],
            "gold_patch": row["patch"],
        }
        work = scratch / f"{row['instance_id']}.{'dated' if dated else 'current'}"
        try:
            checkout(task, work)
            env = environment(task, work, work.parent / f"{work.name}.venv")
            files = changed(row["test_patch"])
            apply(work, row["test_patch"])
            before = tests(work, env, files)
            apply(work, row["patch"])
            after = tests(work, env, files)
        except (RuntimeError, subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError) as error:
            reason = f"setup: {error}"
            continue
        if not f2p or any(after.get(t) != "PASSED" for t in f2p):
            reason = "gold patch does not pass fail-to-pass here"
        elif any(before.get(t) == "PASSED" for t in f2p):
            reason = "fail-to-pass already passes on the base commit"
        else:
            task["fail_to_pass"] = f2p
            task["pass_to_pass"] = [t for t in p2p if before.get(t) == "PASSED" == after.get(t)]
            task["test_files"] = files
            return task
    return reason


def verify(candidates: Path, jobs: int, only: list[str]) -> None:
    rows = [r for r in json.loads(candidates.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))]
    rows = [r for r in rows if not only or r["instance_id"] in only]
    scratch = CACHE / "verify"
    shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)
    scratch.mkdir(parents=True)
    kept: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(jobs) as pool:
        for row, result in zip(rows, pool.map(lambda r: verify_one(r, scratch), rows), strict=True):
            if isinstance(result, str):
                print(f"drop {row['instance_id']}: {result}")
            else:
                print(
                    f"keep {row['instance_id']}: {len(result['fail_to_pass'])} f2p, "
                    f"{len(result['pass_to_pass'])} p2p"
                )
                kept.append(result)
    kept.sort(key=order)
    TASKS.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    TASKS.write_text(json.dumps({"dataset": DATASET, "tasks": kept}, indent=1) + "\n", "utf-8")
    print(f"{len(kept)} of {len(rows)} instances verified -> {TASKS}")
