# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost cap.** `--max-tokens N` caps billed-equivalent tokens (input, output, cache read and
  cache write, unweighted). Admission is projected: until a run reports its cost only one run is
  in flight; after that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every in-flight run at the
  largest observed cost fits. Realized spend can still exceed the cap by one run's cost when a
  run's cost is larger than any seen before. The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k
  against a 450k cap; that file is kept as evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

Amendment 5, before any held-out look (review of PR #52): (1) every `git` command on the agent's
tree, including `git apply` of the hidden test patch and the editable install's build hooks, runs
under the same bubblewrap confinement; a planted clean filter no longer runs on the host (tests
in `tests/python/test_agent_run.py` and `test_agent_environment.py`). (2) `/run` and `/var/run`
are masked so host sockets (docker, systemd) are unreachable; name-service files are re-bound.
(3) Run artifacts are written with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` after unlinking, and a symlinked OpenCode
credential database is removed, never opened. (4) Pytest infrastructure failures (timeout, launch
failure, exit 3/4) are harness errors, not unresolved tasks; a broken collection is the agent's
result. (5) `report` prints `provisional` unless the adjacent manifest's whole task x arm x
repetition matrix is scored, or when the manifest is missing. Residuals: the agent and build hooks
keep network access, the hidden-test pytest runs the agent's own `conftest.py` (it could forge
`PASSED` lines), test files are restored from the agent-writable `.git`, and sockets outside
`/run` (for example abstract or `/tmp/.X11-unix`) are not filtered.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost cap.** `--max-tokens N` caps billed-equivalent tokens (input, output, cache read and
  cache write, unweighted). Admission is projected: until a run reports its cost only one run is
  in flight; after that a run starts only if the spend so far plus every in-flight run at the
  largest observed cost fits. Realized spend can still exceed the cap by one run's cost when a
  run's cost is larger than any seen before. The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k
  against a 450k cap; that file is kept as evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

Amendment 5, before any held-out look (review of PR #52): (1) every `git` command on the agent's
tree, including `git apply` of the hidden test patch and the editable install's build hooks, runs
under the same bubblewrap confinement; a planted clean filter no longer runs on the host (tests
in `tests/python/test_agent_run.py` and `test_agent_environment.py`). (2) `/run` and `/var/run`
are masked so host sockets (docker, systemd) are unreachable; name-service files are re-bound.
(3) Run artifacts are written with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` after unlinking, and a symlinked OpenCode
credential database is removed, never opened. (4) On the agent's tree only a failed bubblewrap
launch is a harness error; a hang, a broken `conftest.py` or a collection error is the agent's
unresolved result (gold-patch verification stays strict). (5) `report` prints `provisional` unless the
adjacent manifest's whole task x arm x
repetition matrix is scored, or when the manifest is missing. Residuals: the agent and build hooks
keep network access, the hidden-test pytest runs the agent's own `conftest.py` (it could forge
`PASSED` lines), test files are restored from the agent-writable `.git`, and sockets outside
`/run` (for example abstract or `/tmp/.X11-unix`) are not filtered.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

"""Runner regressions: confined git, private traces, nested credentials, base-src, scoring."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import importlib
import json
import os
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import pytest

SCRIPTS = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "agent_eval")
if SCRIPTS not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPTS)

arms: Any = importlib.import_module("arms")
batch: Any = importlib.import_module("batch")
events: Any = importlib.import_module("events")
run: Any = importlib.import_module("run")
session: Any = importlib.import_module("session")
tasks: Any = importlib.import_module("tasks")


def _git_missing(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.CompletedProcess((), 1)


def test_base_src_package_snapshot_imports(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    pkg = tmp_path / "oxide"
    pkg.mkdir()
    (pkg / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (pkg / "__main__.py").write_text("print('base-ok')\n", encoding="utf-8")
    done = subprocess.run(
        arms.oxide_command("oxide-base", pkg, "--version"),
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        check=False,
    )
    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr
    assert "base-ok" in done.stdout


def test_base_src_tree_containing_the_package_imports(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    root = tmp_path / "src"
    pkg = root / "oxide"
    pkg.mkdir(parents=True)
    (pkg / "__init__.py").write_text("", encoding="utf-8")
    (pkg / "__main__.py").write_text("print('tree-ok')\n", encoding="utf-8")
    done = subprocess.run(
        arms.oxide_command("oxide-base", root), capture_output=True, text=True, check=False
    )
    assert done.returncode == 0, done.stderr
    assert "tree-ok" in done.stdout


def test_base_src_rejects_a_directory_that_is_not_the_package(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="src/oxide"):
        arms.check_base_src(tmp_path)


def test_the_manifest_builds_for_every_arm_without_a_base_snapshot() -> None:
    args = argparse.Namespace(
        split="dev",
        reps=1,
        model="m",
        timeout=1,
        arms=list(arms.ARMS),
        base_src=None,
        runner="opencode",
    )
    assert batch.manifest(args, [{"id": "a"}])["tasks"] == 1


def test_nested_credential_json_is_extracted_for_redaction(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    key, access, refresh = (
        "REDACTED",
        "access-token-0123",
        "refresh-token-0123",
    )
    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    blob = json.dumps({"key": key, "access": access, "refresh": refresh})
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', ?)", (blob,))
    secrets = run.credential_values(db)
    assert key in secrets and access in secrets and refresh in secrets
    assert key not in run.confine.redact(f"used {key} and {access}", secrets)


def test_a_plain_credential_string_is_still_extracted(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    key = "REDACTED"
    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', ?)", (key,))
    assert key in run.credential_values(db)


def test_git_on_agent_tree_is_confined(tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}
    ran: tuple[str, ...] = ()

    def confine_fn(argv: list[str], *, writable: Path, hide: object, net: bool) -> list[str]:
        seen["argv"] = list(argv)
        seen["net"] = net
        seen["writable"] = writable
        return ["bwrap", *map(str, argv)]

    def sh(*argv: str, **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        nonlocal ran
        ran = argv
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0)

    monkeypatch.setattr(session.confine, "confine", confine_fn)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "hidden", lambda: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "sh", sh)
    base = tmp_path / "base"
    work = base / "work"
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    session.git_on_agent(base, "add", "-A", cwd=work)
    assert seen["argv"] == ["git", *session.GIT_SAFE, "add", "-A"]
    assert seen["net"] is False
    assert seen["writable"] == base
    assert ran[0] == "bwrap"


def test_score_confines_git_and_counts_a_missing_test_as_unresolved(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    calls: list[tuple[str, ...]] = []

    def git(base: Path, *args: str, cwd: Path) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        calls.append(args)
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(args, 0)

    def sh(*argv: str, **kwargs: object) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        assert argv[0] != "git"
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0)

    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "git_on_agent", git)
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "sh", sh)
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "apply", lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "tests", lambda *args, **kwargs: {"t": "PASSED"})
    task = {
        "test_files": ["t.py"],
        "test_patch": "",
        "fail_to_pass": ["t"],
        "pass_to_pass": ["missing"],
    }
    scored = session.score(task, tmp_path, {}, tmp_path)
    assert scored == {"resolved": False, "f2p_failed": 0, "p2p_broken": 1}
    assert calls[0][:2] == ("cat-file", "-e")
    assert "checkout" in calls[1]


def test_score_does_not_turn_a_test_runner_error_into_a_result(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "git_on_agent", _git_missing)
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "apply", lambda *args, **kwargs: None)

    def boom(*args: object, **kwargs: object) -> dict[str, str]:
        raise tasks.TestRunError("pytest timed out")

    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "tests", boom)
    task = {"test_files": [], "test_patch": "", "fail_to_pass": ["t"], "pass_to_pass": []}
    with pytest.raises(tasks.TestRunError, match="timed out"):
        session.score(task, tmp_path, {}, tmp_path)


def test_a_reported_test_failure_is_still_unresolved(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setattr(session, "git_on_agent", _git_missing)
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "apply", lambda *args, **kwargs: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(session.tasks, "tests", lambda *args, **kwargs: {"t": "FAILED"})
    task = {"test_files": [], "test_patch": "", "fail_to_pass": ["t"], "pass_to_pass": []}
    assert session.score(task, tmp_path, {}, tmp_path)["resolved"] is False


def test_trace_write_does_not_truncate_a_hardlink(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    victim = tmp_path / "victim"
    victim.write_text("keep", encoding="utf-8")
    link = tmp_path / "patch.diff"
    os.link(victim, link)
    session.write_private(link, "diff")
    assert victim.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "keep"
    assert link.read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "diff"


@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="creating a symlink needs extra privileges")
def test_run_one_confines_git_and_does_not_follow_trace_links(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    victim = tmp_path / "victim"

@pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("bwrap") is None, reason="bubblewrap not installed")
def test_a_planted_git_clean_filter_cannot_write_outside_the_confined_tree() -> None:
    # Under $HOME, not /tmp: confine mounts a tmpfs over /tmp, which would hide the marker.
    scratch = Path.home() / ".cache" / f"oxide-filter-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    base, marker = scratch / "base", scratch / "escaped"
    work = base / "work"
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        env = {**os.environ, "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": os.devnull, "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM": os.devnull}
        for argv in (["init", "-q"], ["config", "filter.plant.clean", f"touch {marker}; cat"]):
            subprocess.run(["git", *argv], cwd=work, check=True, env=env)
        (work / ".gitattributes").write_text("* filter=plant\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "f.txt").write_text("x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        # Control: unconfined, the same tree runs the planted filter on the host.
        subprocess.run(["git", *session.GIT_SAFE, "add", "-A"], cwd=work, check=True, env=env)
        assert marker.exists()
        marker.unlink()
        (work / ".git" / "index").unlink()
        session.git_on_agent(base, "add", "-A", cwd=work)
        assert not marker.exists()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)

def test_a_planted_clean_filter_does_not_run_on_the_host_when_the_test_patch_is_applied() -> None:
    scratch = Path.home() / ".cache" / f"oxide-apply-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    base, marker = scratch / "base", scratch / "escaped"
    work = base / "work"
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    patch = "--- a/f.txt\n+++ b/f.txt\n@@ -1 +1 @@\n-x\n+y\n"
    try:
        env = {**os.environ, "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": os.devnull, "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM": os.devnull}
        for argv in (["init", "-q"], ["config", "filter.plant.clean", f"touch {marker}; cat"]):
            subprocess.run(["git", *argv], cwd=work, check=True, env=env)
        (work / ".gitattributes").write_text("* filter=plant\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "f.txt").write_text("x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        tasks.apply(work, patch)  # control: unconfined, the filter runs on the host
        assert marker.exists()
        marker.unlink()
        (work / "f.txt").write_text("x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        tasks.apply(work, patch, wrap=session.confined(base, net=False), scratch=base)
        assert not marker.exists()
        assert (work / "f.txt").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "y\n"
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)

def test_a_planted_git_clean_filter_cannot_write_outside_the_confined_tree() -> None:
    # Under $HOME, not /tmp: confine mounts a tmpfs over /tmp, which would hide the marker.
    scratch = Path.home() / ".cache" / f"oxide-filter-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    base, marker = scratch / "base", scratch / "escaped"
    work = base / "work"
    work.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        env = {**os.environ, "GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL": os.devnull, "GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM": os.devnull}
        for argv in (["init", "-q"], ["config", "filter.plant.clean", f"touch {marker}; cat"]):
            subprocess.run(["git", *argv], cwd=work, check=True, env=env)
        (work / ".gitattributes").write_text("* filter=plant\n", encoding="utf-8")
        (work / "f.txt").write_text("x\n", encoding="utf-8")
        # Control: unconfined, the same tree runs the planted filter on the host.
        subprocess.run(["git", *session.GIT_SAFE, "add", "-A"], cwd=work, check=True, env=env)
        assert marker.exists()
        marker.unlink()
        (work / ".git" / "index").unlink()
        session.git_on_agent(base, "add", "-A", cwd=work)
        assert not marker.exists()
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(scratch, ignore_errors=True)

def test_a_dangling_name_service_link_refuses_to_start(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = tmp_path / "run"
    runtime.mkdir()
    link = tmp_path / "resolv.conf"
    _symlink(link, runtime / "missing.conf")

def test_a_runtime_directory_is_not_bound_back(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    runtime = tmp_path / "run"
    runtime.mkdir()
    link = tmp_path / "resolv.conf"
    _symlink(link, runtime)
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="runtime sockets"):
        confine.socket_mounts([runtime], [link])


def test_a_symlink_runtime_dir_is_not_a_mount_point(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    real = tmp_path / "run"
    real.mkdir()
    link = tmp_path / "var-run"
    _symlink(link, real)
    assert confine.runtime_dirs((real, link)) == [real]

tasks: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("tasks")


def task(**extra: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "id": "psf__requests-1",
        "repo": "psf/requests",
        "version": "2.0",
        "created_at": "2026-08-01T00:00:00Z",
        "dated": True,
        **extra,
    }


@pytest.fixture
def commands(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> list[list[str]]:
    seen: list[list[str]] = []

    def fake_sh(*argv: str, **_: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        seen.append(list(argv))
        return subprocess.CompletedProcess(argv, 0, "", "")

    monkeypatch.setattr(tasks, "sh", fake_sh)
    monkeypatch.setattr(tasks.confine, "require", lambda: None)
    return seen


def test_a_dev_task_keeps_the_frozen_recipe(commands: list[list[str]]) -> None:
    tasks.environment(task(), Path("/w"), Path("/v"))
    assert ["uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", "3.9", Path("/v")] in commands
    assert any("setuptools<70" in argv for argv in commands)


def test_a_held_out_build_replaces_python_and_setuptools(commands: list[list[str]]) -> None:
    build = {"python": "3.12", "setuptools": "setuptools>=77"}
    tasks.environment(task(build=build), Path("/w"), Path("/v"))
    assert ["uv", "venv", "-q", "--python", "3.12", Path("/v")] in commands
    assert any("setuptools>=77" in argv for argv in commands)
    assert not any("setuptools<70" in argv for argv in commands)


def test_the_editable_install_cannot_run_build_hooks_on_the_host(
    commands: list[list[str]],
) -> None:
    tasks.environment(task(), Path("/w"), Path("/v"))
    editable = next(argv for argv in commands if "-e" in argv)
    assert editable[0] == "bwrap"
    assert "--unshare-net" not in editable
    die = editable.index("--die-with-parent")
    assert editable[die - 3 : die] == ["--bind", "/v", "/v"]
    assert ["--bind", "/w", "/w"] in [editable[i : i + 3] for i in range(len(editable) - 2)]
    assert str(tasks.ROOT / "fixtures" / "eval") in editable
    assert all(argv[0] != "bwrap" for argv in commands if "-e" not in argv)


def test_a_timeout_is_not_a_test_result(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    def fake_sh(*argv: str, **_: Any) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
        raise subprocess.TimeoutExpired(list(argv), 1)

    monkeypatch.setattr(tasks, "sh", fake_sh)
    with pytest.raises(tasks.TestRunError, match="timed out"):
        tasks.tests(Path("/w"), {}, ["tests/test_a.py"], timeout=1)

"""The agent's process is confined: no host secrets in its environment, the answers and other runs
hidden from its filesystem, and its kept traces free of the credential it used. Behaviour is
checked with the real bubblewrap where it is installed, and the rest with pure functions."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import itertools
import shutil
import sqlite3
import subprocess
import sys
import uuid
from collections.abc import Generator
from contextlib import contextmanager
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType
from typing import Any

import pytest

SCRIPTS = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "agent_eval")
if SCRIPTS not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPTS)

confine: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("confine")
run: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("run")
tasks: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("tasks")

BWRAP = pytest.mark.skipif(shutil.which("bwrap") is None, reason="bubblewrap not installed")


@contextmanager
def home_scratch() -> Generator[Path, None, None]:
    """A directory under $HOME, not /tmp: confine mounts a tmpfs over /tmp, which would hide it
    for the wrong reason."""
    path = Path.home() / ".cache" / f"oxide-confine-test-{uuid.uuid4().hex}"
    path.mkdir(parents=True)
    try:
        yield path
    finally:
        shutil.rmtree(path, ignore_errors=True)


def test_the_agent_environment_holds_no_host_api_key(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("OPENAI_API_KEY", "REDACTED")
    monkeypatch.setenv("GITHUB_TOKEN", "ghp_0123456789abcdef")
    env = confine.clean_env({"HOME": "/h"})
    assert "OPENAI_API_KEY" not in env and "GITHUB_TOKEN" not in env
    assert env["HOME"] == "/h"


def test_the_runner_passes_the_agent_only_the_clean_environment(
    monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, tmp_path: Path
) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", "REDACTED")
    seen: dict[str, Any] = {}

    def fake_launch(
        command: list[str], cwd: Path, environment: dict[str, str], timeout: int
    ) -> tuple[str, str]:
        seen["environment"] = environment
        return "ok", ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "launch", fake_launch)
    monkeypatch.setattr(confine, "require", lambda: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "credentials", lambda *_: None)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "credential_values", lambda *_: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "forget_credentials", lambda *_: None)
    base = tmp_path / "base"
    (base / "work").mkdir(parents=True)
    run.agent("openai/m", "control", {"problem": "p"}, base, {"PATH": "/venv/bin"}, 1)
    assert "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY" not in seen["environment"]


def test_without_bubblewrap_no_agent_is_started(monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:
    monkeypatch.setenv("PATH", "/nonexistent")
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="bubblewrap"):
        confine.confine(["true"], writable=Path("/tmp"), hide=(), net=False)


@BWRAP
def test_a_hidden_path_cannot_be_read_and_the_writable_one_can() -> None:
    with home_scratch() as root:
        answers = root / "answers"
        answers.mkdir()
        (answers / "gold.patch").write_text("secret", encoding="utf-8")
        work = root / "work"
        work.mkdir()
        read = confine.confine(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; open(sys.argv[1]).read()", answers / "gold.patch"],
            writable=work,
            hide=(answers,),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(read, capture_output=True).returncode != 0
        write = confine.confine(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; open(sys.argv[1], 'w').write('ok')", work / "f"],
            writable=work,
            hide=(answers,),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(write, capture_output=True).returncode == 0
        assert (work / "f").read_text(encoding="utf-8") == "ok"


@BWRAP
def test_a_path_outside_the_writable_dir_cannot_be_written() -> None:
    with home_scratch() as root:
        work, other = root / "work", root / "other"
        work.mkdir()
        other.mkdir()
        argv = confine.confine(
            [sys.executable, "-c", "import sys; open(sys.argv[1], 'w')", other / "x"],
            writable=work,
            hide=(),
            net=False,
        )
        assert subprocess.run(argv, capture_output=True).returncode != 0


def test_redaction_removes_a_secret_from_kept_text() -> None:
    key = "REDACTED"
    assert confine.redact(f"auth {key} done", [key]) == "auth [redacted] done"


def test_forgetting_credentials_empties_the_kept_copy(tmp_path: Path) -> None:
    db = tmp_path / "opencode.db"
    with sqlite3.connect(db) as conn:
        conn.execute("CREATE TABLE credential (integration_id TEXT, value TEXT)")
        conn.execute("INSERT INTO credential VALUES ('openai', 'REDACTED')")
    run.forget_credentials(db)

PR #52 is fixed on the CI side. I pushed three commits to `feat/secure-agent-eval-harness`, and the head is now `0b1c809`. The platform jobs and `Verify` all pass. Two checks still fail, and I can't fix either from this branch.

**What failed on the first push (`9a0287e`):**
- **Manifest test, all platforms:** my new `test_the_manifest_builds_for_every_arm_without_a_base_snapshot` ran `opencode --version`, and CI has no `opencode` binary. It passed on my machine only because `opencode` was installed there. I stubbed `batch.runner_version` in `0dfa6f6`.
- **Windows, bind-argument test:** the bind arguments came out as `\v` instead of `/v`. I now compare against `str(Path(...))`.
- **Windows, link test:** `test_a_dangling_name_service_link_refuses_to_start` needs bubblewrap, which doesn't exist on Windows. I skip it there. Both Windows fixes are in `0b1c809`.

**What passes now:** `linux-x86_64` (plain, py3.12 and py3.14), `macos-arm64`, `windows-x86_64`, `Verify`, CodeQL, Analyze (all three), and `classify`.

**What still fails:**
- **Risk-tiered review:** the CI reviewer was denied read access to the diff file `oxide-pr.diff`, so it reviewed none of the code. It then returned `blocking_findings: true` because the review was incomplete. The cause is `.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml`. It grants the reviewer only the inline-comment tool and tells it to read a temp file that tool list can't open. That is a workflow bug, not a problem in this PR. The new intent spec was never examined, so I can't say whether it clears the gate. Fixing it means changing the workflow and re-running the job. I didn't touch the workflow, since you asked me to patch the PR.
- **Entire Gates:** this is an external check at entire.com and gives no description. I can't see why it fails.

**Risk:** the tests I skipped or stubbed for CI (the manifest test and the Windows link test) no longer exercise those paths on those platforms. Real-bwrap coverage runs only where bubblewrap is installed, so none ran in CI.

# Oxide Conventions

> Generated from [Kiy-K/oxide](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide) on 2026-09-03

## Overview

This skill teaches Claude the development patterns and conventions used in oxide.

## Tech Stack

- **Language**: Python 3.12+ (`src/oxide/`: `api.py`, `models.py`, `core/`, `storage/`, `capture.py`, `cli.py`), managed with uv
- **Architecture**: modular monolith per `docs/spec/SPEC.md`; boundaries in the root `AGENTS.md`
- **Tests**: pytest in `tests/python/`; every test and subprocess gets a private data location
- **Checks**: `mise run verify`

## When to Use This Skill

Activate this skill when:
- Making changes to this repository
- Adding new features following established patterns
- Writing tests that match project conventions
- Creating commits with proper message format

## Commit Conventions

Follow these commit message conventions based on 1 analyzed commits.

### Commit Style: Conventional Commits

### Prefixes Used

- `fix`

### Message Guidelines

- Average message length: ~47 characters
- Keep first line concise and descriptive
- Use imperative mood ("Add feature" not "Added feature")


*Commit message example*

```text
fix(cli): resolve common first-run UX papercuts
```

## Architecture

### Project Structure: Single Package

This project uses **hybrid** module organization.

### Guidelines

- This project uses a hybrid organization
- Follow existing patterns when adding new code

## Code Style

### Language: Python

### Naming Conventions

| Element | Convention |
|---------|------------|
| Modules | snake_case |
| Functions | snake_case |
| Classes | PascalCase |
| Constants | SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE |

### Imports and Exports

Absolute imports from the package (`from oxide.models import ...`), with
`from __future__ import annotations` at the top of each module. The public API is
what `oxide/__init__.py` lists in `__all__` (`docs/public-api.md`).

## Best Practices

Based on analysis of the codebase, follow these practices:

### Do

- Use conventional commit format (feat:, fix:, etc.)
- Type everything for `mypy --strict`

### Don't

- Don't write vague commit messages
- Don't deviate from established patterns without discussion

[.github/workflows/claude-code-review.yml#3699]
1:name: Claude Code Review
2:
3:on:
4:  pull_request_target:
5:    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review, reopened]
6:
7:permissions:
8:  contents: read
9:
10:jobs:
11:  classify:
12:    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
13:    permissions:
14:      contents: read
15:    outputs:
16:      tier: ${{ steps.tier.outputs.tier }}
17:      rubrics: ${{ steps.tier.outputs.rubrics }}
18:    steps:
19:      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
20:        with:
21:          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
22:          fetch-depth: 0
23:          persist-credentials: false
24:      - id: tier
25:        env:
26:          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
27:          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
28:          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
29:        run: |
30:          if git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}:scripts/review_tier.py" 2>/dev/null; then
31:            [[ "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
32:            [[ "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
33:            [[ "$HEAD_REPO" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]
34:            git fetch --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules \
35:              "https://github.com/${HEAD_REPO}.git" "$HEAD_SHA"
36:            python3 scripts/review_tier.py --base "$BASE_SHA" --head "$HEAD_SHA" \
37:              >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
38:          else
39:            # First rollout: no trusted classifier exists in the target branch yet.
40:            printf 'tier=2\nrubrics=docs/review/README.md\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
41:          fi
42:
43:      - name: Materialize exact PR diff
44:        if: steps.tier.outputs.tier != '0'
45:        env:
46:          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
47:          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
48:          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
49:        run: |
50:          [[ "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
51:          [[ "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
52:          [[ "$HEAD_REPO" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]
53:          if ! git cat-file -e "${HEAD_SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
54:            git fetch --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules \
55:              "https://github.com/${HEAD_REPO}.git" "$HEAD_SHA"
56:          fi
57:          git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --binary \
58:            "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" -- > "$RUNNER_TEMP/oxide-pr.diff"
59:
60:      - name: Upload exact PR diff
61:        if: steps.tier.outputs.tier != '0'
62:        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
63:        with:

name: Claude Code Review

on:
  pull_request_target:
    types: [opened, synchronize, ready_for_review, reopened]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  classify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      tier: ${{ steps.tier.outputs.tier }}
      rubrics: ${{ steps.tier.outputs.rubrics }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false
      - id: tier
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
        run: |
          if git cat-file -e "${BASE_SHA}:scripts/review_tier.py" 2>/dev/null; then
            [[ "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
            [[ "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
            [[ "$HEAD_REPO" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]
            git fetch --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules \
              "https://github.com/${HEAD_REPO}.git" "$HEAD_SHA"
            python3 scripts/review_tier.py --base "$BASE_SHA" --head "$HEAD_SHA" \
              >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            # First rollout: no trusted classifier exists in the target branch yet.
            printf 'tier=2\nrubrics=docs/review/README.md\n' >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

      - name: Materialize exact PR diff
        if: steps.tier.outputs.tier != '0'
        env:
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          HEAD_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          HEAD_REPO: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name }}
        run: |
          [[ "$BASE_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
          [[ "$HEAD_SHA" =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{40}$ ]]
          [[ "$HEAD_REPO" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+$ ]]
          if ! git cat-file -e "${HEAD_SHA}^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            git fetch --no-tags --no-recurse-submodules \
              "https://github.com/${HEAD_REPO}.git" "$HEAD_SHA"
          fi
          git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv --no-renames --binary \
            "$BASE_SHA...$HEAD_SHA" -- > "$RUNNER_TEMP/oxide-pr.diff"

      - name: Upload exact PR diff
        if: steps.tier.outputs.tier != '0'
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: oxide-pr-diff-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}/oxide-pr.diff
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 1

  claude-review:
    name: Risk-tiered review
    needs: classify
    if: always()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout trusted base source
        if: needs.classify.result == 'success' && needs.classify.outputs.tier != '0'
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Download exact PR diff
        if: needs.classify.result == 'success' && needs.classify.outputs.tier != '0'
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: oxide-pr-diff-${{ github.run_id }}-${{ github.run_attempt }}
          path: ${{ runner.temp }}

      - name: Run Claude Code Review
        id: claude-review
        if: needs.classify.result == 'success' && needs.classify.outputs.tier != '0'
        uses: anthropics/claude-code-action@v1
        with:
          claude_code_oauth_token: ${{ secrets.CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN }}
          github_token: ${{ github.token }}
          allowed_non_write_users: '*'
          prompt: |
            Review PR #${{ github.event.pull_request.number }} from the exact event snapshot.
            The event's exact PR head was fetched as Git data in a separate contents:read job; no PR
            source is checked out or executed. Review the complete run-scoped diff artifact at
            `${{ runner.temp }}/oxide-pr.diff`; do not fetch live PR metadata or diff. Review tier:
            ${{ needs.classify.outputs.tier }}.
            Apply these OXIDE rubrics from the trusted base: ${{ needs.classify.outputs.rubrics }}.
            Review all relevant changes for BLOCKER and MAJOR findings. For Tier 2 feature or
            behavior changes (not fixes restoring documented behavior), a missing or inadequate
            intent spec in docs/superpowers/specs/ is also blocking. Return blocking_findings=true
            for any blocker, major finding, missing required spec, or incomplete review. Post only
            evidence-backed inline comments.
          claude_args: |
            --allowedTools "mcp__github_inline_comment__create_inline_comment"
            --disallowedTools "Bash,Edit,Write,NotebookEdit"
            --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"blocking_findings":{"type":"boolean"},"summary":{"type":"string"}},"required":["blocking_findings","summary"],"additionalProperties":false}'

      - name: Enforce review gate
        if: always()
        env:
          CLASSIFY_RESULT: ${{ needs.classify.result }}
          REVIEW_TIER: ${{ needs.classify.outputs.tier }}
          REVIEW_CONCLUSION: ${{ steps.claude-review.outputs.conclusion }}
          REVIEW_RESULT: ${{ steps.claude-review.outputs.structured_output }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [[ "$CLASSIFY_RESULT" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "Risk classification failed; refusing to skip review."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "$REVIEW_TIER" == "0" ]]; then
            echo "Tier 0: verification is the only required gate."
            exit 0
          fi
          if [[ "$REVIEW_TIER" != "1" && "$REVIEW_TIER" != "2" ]]; then
            echo "Invalid review tier; refusing to skip review."
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "$REVIEW_CONCLUSION" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "Independent review did not complete successfully."
            exit 1
          fi
          printf '%s' "$REVIEW_RESULT" |
            jq -e 'type == "object" and .blocking_findings == false and (.summary | type == "string")' \
              >/dev/null

30:## Commands
31:
32:[Mise](https://mise.jdx.dev/installing-mise.html) is the one entrypoint;
33:`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
34:installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
35:`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
36:Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).
37:
38:```bash
39:mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
40:                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
41:mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
42:mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
43:mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/

45:```
46:
47:`uv run pyrefly check` is an optional second type checker (`[tool.pyrefly]` in
48:`pyproject.toml`). It is not part of `verify` or CI; mypy `--strict` stays the gate.
49:On 2026-10-31 it reported 32 errors.
50:
51:Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
52:`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
53:stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
54:`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
55:peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
56:in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
57:Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/` at commit `013e791`.
58:`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
59:harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
60:`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
61:frozen `fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); the protocol (splits, gate
62:rules, how to freeze a new version) is in [`fixtures/eval/`](../../fixtures/eval/README.md),
63:and the frozen README states the latest amendment. Gold is audited (`gold-audit.json`); only verified gold is gated.
64:Develop on the dev split; never tune on held-out.
65:`tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` is the same ruler for TypeScript (tasks and gold
66:audit in `fixtures/eval/contextbench-ts/`, latest frozen baseline `baseline-v16/`; corpora in `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench-ts/corpora-v2/`, and the
67:sources-only `corpora/` only reproduces v1). Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate
68:needs ~2 GB of corpora and ~15 minutes, so it is `mise run contextbench-ts`, not part of
69:`verify`. Run it under the limits below before and after any TypeScript retrieval,
70:resolution, routing or packing change.
71:Dependencies live in `pyproject.toml` with a committed `uv.lock`; add them
72:with `uv add`, never by hand-editing the lock. Keep heavy local runs within
73:`CPUQuota=200%`/`MemoryMax=3G` (`systemd-run --user --scope`).
74:To verify another supported Python, set `UV_PYTHON` and a separate
75:`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` for the entire check. `uv sync --python` alone does not
76:carry that interpreter choice into a later `uv run`.
77:
78:OXIDE's engine, CLI, MCP server and distribution need no Node.js, Bun or Rust
79:toolchain. Native Python dependencies are installed as wheels; the Platforms
80:workflow enforces wheel-only third-party installation and runs the installed
81:smoke with only the environment's scripts on `PATH`. That smoke also checks
82:that MCP advertises exactly `oxide_search`. Optional agent tooling (CodeGraph,
83:Context7, archify, external MCP servers) and GitHub Actions have their own runtimes;
84:they are not OXIDE dependencies. See the
85:[legacy infrastructure audit](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) for
86:the inventory and process ancestry.
87:
88:Tests never write to real user data: `tests/python/conftest.py` gives every
89:test a private `OXIDE_DATA_DIR` and XDG locations, fails the session if the
90:real data location changes, and every subprocess receives explicit private
91:locations (`env()` and `python()` there; `env()` refuses any location outside
92:the temporary root). Native probes that could crash, and crash injection, run
93:only in such subprocesses. Lexical tests need the pinned FTS extension
94:(`uv run oxide prepare`, once), and the context-quality gate the corpora
95:(`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py fetch`, once; both are in bootstrap).

98:
99:Commit only when asked. OXIDE v2 lives on `main`; commit there or on a branch
100:from it merged back by PR. Messages use a
101:lowercase prefix plus an imperative summary: `fix:`, `feat:`, `refactor:`,
102:`docs:`, `harden:`, `bench:`, `tierb:`.

104:## Release
105:
106:OXIDE ships to PyPI as `oxide-agent` (PyPI's `oxide` is another project); the import
107:package and the CLI are still `oxide`. Pushing a `v<version>` tag runs

112:One-time setup, before the first tag:

114:1. On PyPI, go to *Your account → Publishing → Add a new pending publisher* and enter:
115:   PyPI project `oxide-agent`, owner `Kiy-K`, repository `oxide`, workflow
116:   `release.yml`, environment `pypi`. The project is created on the first upload.

148:`fixtures/eval/structural-v1/` (Rust retrieval and routing) is a read-only

# OXIDE development workflow

Commands and verification for OXIDE v2, loaded on demand from the root
`AGENTS.md` routing table. Older docs and code comments that cite
"`AGENTS.md`" for a command or harness detail mean this file.

## Default loop

Read the code, change it, add or adjust a test, run `mise run verify`. That is the
whole process for features, fixes, language work and refactors. Only changes that
claim a retrieval/routing/packing quality or performance improvement also need the
ContextBench or `scripts/bench.py` runs below (see `AGENTS.md`).

## Review tiers

Run `mise run tier` on the final diff. It prints `tier=N` and the applicable rubric filenames.
Tiers combine by maximum: unclassified paths default to tier 1; Markdown paths are tier 0 unless a tier-2 path rule matches.

| Tier | Scope | Required before commit |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | Documentation changes, except agent/review/spec policy | `mise run verify` |
| 1 | Tests, ordinary source/configuration paths, and unknown paths | Tier 0 plus an independent zero-context diff review against the printed `docs/review/` rubrics |
| 2 | Public API, capture/storage/core policy, frozen evaluation fixtures, test harness, dependencies, CI/agent configuration, review classifier and architecture authorities | Tier 1 plus a short intent spec in `docs/superpowers/specs/`, reviewed by a zero-context agent before implementation for features/behavior changes. Bug fixes restoring documented behavior do not need a new spec. |

`claude-code-review.yml` is restricted to `pull_request_target`. It checks out only the trusted base commit, fetches the event's exact PR head as Git data, and materializes the immutable diff; it never executes PR code.

Fork reviews use non-write-user mode with best-effort secret scrubbing and comment-only tools; prompt-injection risk is reduced, not eliminated. Classification uses the base branch's copy and defaults to tier 2 during first rollout if the classifier is absent.
CI runs `mise run verify` on every PR. Keep `Verify` required during rollout; after this workflow is deployed and its check succeeds, also require `Risk-tiered review` so setup cannot strand merges. Agents retain autonomous implementation and commits; no per-change human approval is added.

`mise.toml` pins uv, and `.python-version` pins the development Python (uv
installs it). CI (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`) runs exactly `mise run verify`;
`.github/workflows/platforms.yml` runs the suite and an installed-artifact smoke on
Linux, Windows and both macOS architectures ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)).

```bash
mise run bootstrap     # uv sync --locked + `oxide prepare` (pinned FTS extension, sha256-checked)
                       #   + ContextBench corpora at pinned commits (git, cached)
mise run verify        # everything, in order, stopping at the first failure:
mise run lint          #   ruff check + ruff format --check
mise run typecheck     #   mypy --strict over src/ and tests/python/
mise run test          #   pytest (tests/python/)
```

`uv run pyrefly check` is an optional second type checker (`[tool.pyrefly]` in
`pyproject.toml`). It is not part of `verify` or CI; mypy `--strict` stays the gate.
On 2026-10-31 it reported 32 errors.

Use `uv run …` for anything else (`uv run oxide index <path>`, `uv run pytest -k name`).
`uv run oxide mcp --repo <path>` serves the single `oxide_search` tool over stdio (`--http` for
stateless HTTP on loopback); `docs/public-api.md` § MCP has the contract.
`uv run python scripts/bench.py <corpus>` is the reproducible latency and
peak-RSS benchmark: fresh processes and private data, cold and warm definitions
in its docstring, and a JSON report with the corpus identity and environment.
Run it under the limits below; recorded runs are in `docs/migration-audit/bench/` at commit `013e791`.
`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py run [--out DIR]` is the context-quality
harness (entry-point, routing and packing metrics at 256/1,024/4,096 units);
`tests/python/test_contextbench.py` gates it in `mise run verify` against the latest
frozen `fixtures/eval/contextbench-py/baseline-vN/` (`contextbench.BASELINE`); the protocol (splits, gate
rules, how to freeze a new version) is in [`fixtures/eval/`](../../fixtures/eval/README.md),
and the frozen README states the latest amendment. Gold is audited (`gold-audit.json`); only verified gold is gated.
Develop on the dev split; never tune on held-out.
`tests/python/contextbench_ts.py` is the same ruler for TypeScript (tasks and gold
audit in `fixtures/eval/contextbench-ts/`, latest frozen baseline `baseline-v16/`; corpora in `~/.cache/oxide/contextbench-ts/corpora-v2/`, and the
sources-only `corpora/` only reproduces v1). Its scorer cases run in `verify`; the gate
needs ~2 GB of corpora and ~15 minutes, so it is `mise run contextbench-ts`, not part of
`verify`. Run it under the limits below before and after any TypeScript retrieval,
resolution, routing or packing change.
Dependencies live in `pyproject.toml` with a committed `uv.lock`; add them
with `uv add`, never by hand-editing the lock. Keep heavy local runs within
`CPUQuota=200%`/`MemoryMax=3G` (`systemd-run --user --scope`).
To verify another supported Python, set `UV_PYTHON` and a separate
`UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT` for the entire check. `uv sync --python` alone does not
carry that interpreter choice into a later `uv run`.

OXIDE's engine, CLI, MCP server and distribution need no Node.js, Bun or Rust
toolchain. Native Python dependencies are installed as wheels; the Platforms
workflow enforces wheel-only third-party installation and runs the installed
smoke with only the environment's scripts on `PATH`. That smoke also checks
that MCP advertises exactly `oxide_search`. Optional agent tooling (CodeGraph,
Context7, archify, external MCP servers) and GitHub Actions have their own runtimes;
they are not OXIDE dependencies. See the
[legacy infrastructure audit](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/blob/013e7910d6fe8b9df9ba753bd68e2b6468bb4e51/docs/migration-audit/legacy-infrastructure.md) for
the inventory and process ancestry.

Tests never write to real user data: `tests/python/conftest.py` gives every
test a private `OXIDE_DATA_DIR` and XDG locations, fails the session if the
real data location changes, and every subprocess receives explicit private
locations (`env()` and `python()` there; `env()` refuses any location outside
the temporary root). Native probes that could crash, and crash injection, run
only in such subprocesses. Lexical tests need the pinned FTS extension
(`uv run oxide prepare`, once), and the context-quality gate the corpora
(`uv run python tests/python/contextbench.py fetch`, once; both are in bootstrap).

## Commits

Commit only when asked. OXIDE v2 lives on `main`; commit there or on a branch
from it merged back by PR. Messages use a
lowercase prefix plus an imperative summary: `fix:`, `feat:`, `refactor:`,
`docs:`, `harden:`, `bench:`, `tierb:`.

## Release

OXIDE ships to PyPI as `oxide-agent` (PyPI's `oxide` is another project); the import
package and the CLI are still `oxide`. Pushing a `v<version>` tag runs
`.github/workflows/release.yml`. It runs the whole Platforms matrix, Intel macOS
included, and then uploads the wheel and sdist that linux-x86_64 built and smoke-tested.
The upload uses PyPI trusted publishing (OIDC), so no token is stored anywhere.

One-time setup, before the first tag:

1. On PyPI, go to *Your account → Publishing → Add a new pending publisher* and enter:
   PyPI project `oxide-agent`, owner `Kiy-K`, repository `oxide`, workflow
   `release.yml`, environment `pypi`. The project is created on the first upload.
2. On GitHub, go to *Settings → Environments → New environment* and create `pypi`.
   Add yourself as a required reviewer, and limit deployment to tags matching `v*`.

Each release: set `version` in `pyproject.toml`, run `uv lock`, `mise run verify` and
`mise run pythons`, merge to `main`, then tag that commit `v<version>` and push the tag
(only when the release is approved). The publish job fails unless the tag matches the
built version.

## Historical reproduction

Legacy harnesses (`eval-agent/`, `scripts/agent_eval/`, `scripts/perf.sh`) and
completed study reports are not in this checkout. Run them from their pinned tree:
`013e791` for the Phase 6 studies and the last copy of the legacy harnesses,
`ac985b28` for v1, `f79808a` for the replaced Rust/Bun v2 runtime. The legacy
ContextBench evaluator requires Python 3.11; old TS/TSX task verification uses Bun.
Do not apply v1 CLI, embedding or SQLite contracts to the Python engine.

## LadybugDB FTS extension

LadybugDB comes from its Python wheel (`ladybug==0.21.0`, matched to the FTS build; [docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)), so there is no
native build step. Full-text search is a separate native extension: `uv run
oxide prepare` (part of `mise run bootstrap`) downloads this platform's pinned
0.21.0 build ([docs/platforms.md](../platforms.md)) over HTTPS and checks its SHA-256 into
`$XDG_CACHE_HOME/oxide/ladybug-extensions-0.21.0/` (override with
`OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION`). It is the only network access OXIDE makes. The
engine re-verifies the digest before every `LOAD EXTENSION` by path, never
`INSTALL`; without the file the lexical channel reports `unavailable` and
structural retrieval and routing continue. No vector extension exists.

## Frozen baselines

`fixtures/eval/structural-v1/` (Rust retrieval and routing) is a read-only
oracle: `tests/python/test_baseline.py` asserts the Python engine reproduces
it exactly. A pin or version bump that changes it is a new baseline
directory with a recorded comparison, never a regenerated old one.
Earlier Phase 4/5 reports and DecisionBench/JEV harness instructions are in the
[retired runtime tree](https://github.com/Kiy-K/oxide/tree/f79808a/docs), not local
`docs/phase-4/` or `docs/phase-5/` directories. Reproduction requires that tree.

Each language's conformance suite runs in `mise run verify` (`tests/python/test_<language>.py`).
Where a bounded real-repository and ContextBench diagnostic exists, it is `scripts/eval_<language>.py`, with
protocol and results in the pinned `docs/phase-6/<language>-v1/` at `013e791`. Rerun it only when a change claims to
move that language's resolution quality; ordinary fixes need only `verify`.

content.text:
[SECURITY_MODEL.md#5E2B]
1:# Threat model: Kiy-K/oxide (OXIDE v2)
2:
3:This model was built from the code at `main` (2605eea) and from the owner's answers (2026-11-06). No infrastructure repository: oxide is a local tool, distributed as the `oxide-agent` PyPI package. Its only "infrastructure" is the GitHub Actions workflows in `.github/workflows/`.
4:
5:## System overview
6:
7:OXIDE is a local, single-user Python library, CLI, and MCP server. It captures a repository worktree, derives a typed graph of files, modules, symbols, and relations with tree-sitter parsers, persists it in an embedded LadybugDB store under the user's data dir, and answers queries with ranked locations or budgeted source bundles. These bundles are fed to AI coding agents. The query path is offline: no embeddings, no model, no network. Network access happens in exactly two places: `oxide prepare`, which downloads the pinned FTS native extension, and the optional JEV judge, which uploads source excerpts to TypeSafe.
8:
9:## Components
10:
11:| Component | Code | Notes |
12:|---|---|---|
13:| **Capture** | `src/oxide/capture.py`, `src/oxide/tracking.py` | Reads the worktree. No symlink following, no special files, gitignore handling, size limits (1 MiB/file, 1 GiB total). Uses a watchfiles freshness thread. |
14:| **Parsers** | `src/oxide/core/languages/*`, `src/oxide/core/indexing.py`, `structural.py` | Tree-sitter derivation for Python/TS/JS/Go/Rust/Java/C/C++. Also tsconfig and Cargo.toml resolution. Handles fully untrusted repo content. |
15:| **Retrieval** | `src/oxide/core/retrieval.py`, `routing.py`, `navigation.py`, `packing.py`, `capsule.py`, `ordering.py` | Query terms, TreeRouter, selection and packing of source into bundles. |
16:| **Storage** | `src/oxide/storage/` (`store.py`, `ladybug.py`, `fts.py`), `src/oxide/_index.py` | LadybugDB generations, store lock, publication, Cypher queries, loading the FTS native extension, digest checks. |
17:| **API/CLI** | `src/oxide/api.py`, `models.py`, `cli.py` | Public Python API and `oxide` CLI. |
18:| **MCP server** | `src/oxide/mcp_server.py` | FastMCP `oxide_search` over stdio, or stateless HTTP restricted to loopback. Optional `--repo` allowlist. |
