# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost threshold.** `--max-tokens N` uses recorded billed-equivalent tokens (input, output,
  cache read and cache write, unweighted) for projected admission. Capped runs are serialized;
  a new run starts only if its estimated cost fits the remaining threshold. A single run can
  exceed the threshold: this is not a hard provider-enforced budget or a per-run token limit.
  The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k against a 450k cap; that file is kept as
  evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. Each Codex copy of the login is
deleted when its run ends, so kept traces do not hold it.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed, each covered by a test in `tests/python/test_agent_confine.py`: (1)
`forget_credentials` deleted the OpenCode credential row but left the key in SQLite free pages; it
now runs `VACUUM`. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

Amendment 5, before any held-out look (review of PR #52): (1) every `git` command on the agent's
tree, including `git apply` of the hidden test patch and the editable install's build hooks, runs
under the same bubblewrap confinement; a planted clean filter no longer runs on the host (tests
in `tests/python/test_agent_run.py` and `test_agent_environment.py`). (2) `/run` and `/var/run`
are masked so host sockets (docker, systemd) are unreachable; name-service files are re-bound.
(3) Run artifacts are written with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` after unlinking, and a symlinked OpenCode
credential database is removed, never opened. (4) On the agent's tree only a failed bubblewrap
launch is a harness error; a hang, a broken `conftest.py` or a collection error is the agent's
unresolved result (gold-patch verification stays strict). (5) `report` prints `provisional` unless the
adjacent manifest's whole task x arm x
repetition matrix is scored, or when the manifest is missing. Residuals: the agent and build hooks
keep network access, the hidden-test pytest runs the agent's own `conftest.py` (it could forge
`PASSED` lines), test files are restored from the agent-writable `.git`, and sockets outside
`/run` (for example abstract or `/tmp/.X11-unix`) are not filtered.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

# Agent task-success evaluation (OXIDE vs no-OXIDE)

Question: does giving a coding agent OXIDE's `oxide mcp` tool raise the share of real bugs it
fixes, against the same agent without it? SPEC § Evaluation (System) asks for this: fixed
agent, model, tools and task snapshot, with a no-OXIDE control. Written before any result was
read; change it only with a new version of this file.

## Tasks

`tasks.json`: instances of [SWE-bench Verified](https://huggingface.co/datasets/princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified)
(revision pinned in the file) from the repositories `scripts/agent_eval/tasks.py` can build
(`REPOS`). `verify` keeps an instance only if, in a fresh environment at its base commit, every
fail-to-pass test fails before and passes after the gold patch. Its pass-to-pass set is the
tests that pass both before and after, so an environment difference cannot count against an arm.
The agent gets a one-commit checkout (no history, no remote), the issue text, and a ready
virtualenv. Web fetch and search, skills and questions are denied in both arms.

Run order is fixed: tasks sorted by `sha256(instance id)`, the first `--tasks N` of them.

## Arms

| | tools |
|---|---|
| `control` | the agent's built-ins only |
| `oxide` | the same, plus `oxide mcp --repo <checkout>`, indexed before the clock starts |

The prompt is identical except that the `oxide` arm adds one sentence naming the tool. The
agent is `opencode run --standalone` in an isolated config directory (no user MCP servers,
skills or plugins), one pinned model for both arms. The model must come from an API-backed
provider: `claude-agent/*` runs inside the user's Claude Code and loads that account's MCP
servers (a CodeGraph tool appeared in the control arm), so it is not a clean control. The tool
list of each arm was checked before the run. Runs interleave in a shuffled but seeded order.

**Pinned for run 1:** model `openai/gpt-5.6-luna`, the first 20 tasks, 3 repetitions per task
and arm (120 runs), 1,200 s per run. A 4-run pilot (2 tasks, 1 repetition, both arms resolved)
only exercised the harness and is excluded from the results.

## Measures

A run is **resolved** when, after the agent stops, the hidden tests pass: every fail-to-pass test
and every verified pass-to-pass test, with the agent's own test edits reverted. Per task, the
resolve rate is the share of resolved repetitions in each arm. The effect is the mean over tasks of
`rate(oxide) - rate(control)`, with a 95% percentile bootstrap over tasks (10,000 resamples,
seed 0). Also reported, not gated: median wall time, output tokens and steps, whether the agent
called the tool, and the index time.

## Rule

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost threshold.** `--max-tokens N` uses recorded billed-equivalent tokens (input, output,
  cache read and cache write, unweighted) for projected admission. Capped runs are serialized;
  a new run starts only if its estimated cost fits the remaining threshold. A single run can
  exceed the threshold: this is not a hard provider-enforced budget or a per-run token limit.
  The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k against a 450k cap; that file is kept as
  evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
  Treat traces as sensitive: literal redaction cannot remove copied, encoded or refreshed secrets.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.

OXIDE **improves task success** only if the lower bound of that interval is above 0. Otherwise
the record says "no demonstrated improvement" with the observed interval, whatever the point
estimate. Harness errors (checkout, install, index) are excluded and listed; more than 10% of
runs erroring voids the run. A positive result is a claim about this model, these tasks and
this tool surface, not about agents in general.

## Known limits

- The model may have seen these public issues and fixes in training; the paired design cancels
  it only if it helps both arms equally.
- Tasks are single-repository Python bugs in small to mid-size codebases, where search is
  cheapest without OXIDE.
- Repetitions are independent samples of one stochastic agent; with 20 tasks the interval
  resolves only large effects.


## Run 3 results (amendment)

Run 3 used all 29 tasks in `tasks.json`, 3 repetitions per arm, and the settings above.
The latest 174 attempts scored with no harness errors after 16 provider-auth failures were
retried. Control resolved 47/87 runs; OXIDE resolved 49/87. The task-mean paired difference
was +0.023, with a 95% task-bootstrap interval of [-0.023, +0.080] (better/worse/tied:
2/1/26). The interval includes zero: **no demonstrated improvement**. OXIDE's tool was
called in 19/87 runs (21.8%). Median wall time was 80 s in both arms; median output tokens
were 1,951 control and 2,197 OXIDE.

The nine tasks not included in the original 20-task protocol were also evaluated as a
predeclared additional subset, not newly authored tasks: control resolved 14/27 and OXIDE
15/27; paired difference +0.037, 95% interval [-0.111, +0.222] (better/worse/tied: 1/1/7).
The tool was called in 3/27 OXIDE runs. This subset is too small to establish a gain.

Raw attempts: `~/.cache/oxide/agent-eval/results/run3-reauth-20261106.jsonl`. The evaluator
isolated OpenCode configuration, task worktrees and connected MCP servers, but did not
OS-sandbox agent processes; agents could access the host filesystem. Results apply only to
this model, these public Python tasks and this tool surface. Command and aggregate verdict:
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

## Protocol v2 (amendment)

Changes made after the run 3 diagnosis, recorded before any new result is read. Protocol id
`agent-swe-v2` (`scripts/agent_eval/protocol.py`).

- **Splits.** `dev` is `tasks.json`: the 29 SWE-bench Verified tasks every run to date has used,
  so it is spent and only used for tuning and diagnosis. `heldout` is `heldout-tasks.json`:
  pull requests merged on or after 2026-08-01, selected by the frozen rule in its module.
  A held-out set is opened once with `--final`; a second results file on the same set is refused.
- **Build recipes.** A task may carry `build: {python, setuptools}`. Held-out tasks do, because
  the frozen REPOS recipe fails on current PRs. Their fail-to-pass tests were verified with that
  recipe, and the agent receives the same one. Dev tasks keep the REPOS recipe.
- **Cost threshold.** `--max-tokens N` uses recorded billed-equivalent tokens (input, output,
  cache read and cache write, unweighted) for projected admission. Capped runs are serialized;
  a new run starts only if its estimated cost fits the remaining threshold. A single run can
  exceed the threshold: this is not a hard provider-enforced budget or a per-run token limit.
  The first v2 pilot had no projection and spent 809k against a 450k cap; that file is kept as
  evidence (`results/pilot-v2-smoke.jsonl`).
- **Manifest.** Each results file writes `<results>.manifest.json`: split, task-file and task-id
  hashes, model, prompt and arm-configuration hashes, the opencode version, and a hash of the
  engine and harness source (HEAD, uncommitted edits, untracked files). Resuming under a changed
  manifest is refused, so a results file never mixes two protocols or two code states.
- **Traces.** Each row names its run directory (`trace`), the events hash, its `spend`, and
  `oxide_tools_connected`, which is read from the agent's own log. A run that never calls a
  connected tool is recorded as ignoring it; a run where the tool never connected is a different
  finding. Trace directories are kept, not pruned: events, patch, and OpenCode and OXIDE data.
  Treat traces as sensitive: literal redaction cannot remove copied, encoded or refreshed secrets.
- **Diagnosis.** `scripts/agent_eval diagnose RESULTS` classifies each OXIDE-arm run from its trace
  against the gold patch's files, with the decision rule in `diagnose.py`.

The held-out set is not used for any change until the change is fixed and recorded. Results from
the dev set are for diagnosis and must not be reported as held-out results.

## Discoverability pilot (amendment, pre-registered)

Changed: the `oxide_search` tool description and server instructions in
`src/oxide/mcp_server.py`. Nothing else: model, prompt, tools, budget and task order are the
same. Arms: `oxide` (the new description) and `oxide-base` (a snapshot of the previous source,
`run --base-src`). Their tree hashes are in the manifest. Dev tasks only (`--split dev`, which
is spent and used here only to choose and screen a change): the first 8 in the predeclared
order, 2 repetitions, 1,200 s per run, `--max-tokens 6000000`.

Decision rule, fixed before any result is read. Amended once, before any result: the first two
attempts failed at authorization and produced no resolve data. The rule first written kept a
change whose tool calls rose with flat success. That is the call-frequency target this pilot is
meant to avoid, so the rule now keys on success alone.

1. Invalid if the report's harness-error or provider-auth check fails.
2. Primary measure: the paired resolve-rate difference `oxide - oxide-base` over paired tasks,
   with its bootstrap interval.
3. Keep the change only if the point estimate is above 0. A zero or negative estimate reverts
   it, whatever the tool-call counts. Tool calls are reported to explain the result, not to
   decide it.
4. A kept change is not a success claim. Eight tasks and two repetitions cannot exclude a
   large gain or loss. Success claims need the dev repeats or the one held-out look.

Token spend is recorded, not gated. Traces are kept under the cache.

Amendment 2, before any pilot result (approved by the user): the pinned OpenAI credential in
OpenCode returns HTTP 400 for every model (`openai/gpt-5.6-luna` and `openai/gpt-6-luna` both
fail on a one-word call). The pilot therefore runs through the Codex CLI (`codex exec --json`,
ChatGPT login, isolated `CODEX_HOME` with only `auth.json` copied, `--ignore-user-config`,
`--ephemeral`, workspace-write sandbox) on model `gpt-6-luna`. The decision rule above is
unchanged. The 32 runs of attempt 2 are invalid (provider auth) and are not results. Run-3
OpenCode numbers are not comparable to this pilot; the comparison is paired within Codex.
For Codex, `oxide_tools_connected` is the configured count: Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP
startup. Tool calls are observed. `deny` is not recorded for Codex: it is an OpenCode config
policy, and Codex runs under its `workspace-write` sandbox instead. The original Codex login copy
is removed after a normal run; the agent can still copy or transmit it during execution.

Amendment 3, before any pilot result under this harness (recorded by the user's request to secure
the harness): every agent process and the hidden-test pytest run are confined with bubblewrap
(`scripts/agent_eval/confine.py`). The host is read-only; `fixtures/eval`, the task caches and
bare mirrors (which hold upstream fix commits and other runs' patches), and the host's credential
stores are hidden; only the run directory is writable. Agents inherit an allowlisted environment
with no API keys. The kept OpenCode copy's credential row is deleted after each run and the
credential is redacted from events. Git on the agent's tree runs with hooks and fsmonitor off.
Both arms run under the same confinement, so the comparison stays paired. Runs before this
amendment were not confined and are not comparable to pilot runs.

Amendment 4, verified before any held-out look (credential isolation for Codex and OpenCode). Three
gaps were found and fixed: (1) deleting the OpenCode credential row left the key in SQLite free
pages; cleanup originally used `VACUUM` and now truncates the pinned database inode to avoid
agent-controlled path traversal. (2) The hidden list held a checkout's own `.git`, but a linked worktree's `.git`
is only a pointer, so the shared object store (dev answers, older held-out results) was readable. It
now hides the common git directory and every checkout's `fixtures/eval`, which also covers the
protocol worktree's copy of the held-out set. (3) The agent's tree is a standalone `git init` from
the task archive, so hiding the shared store does not touch it.

Verified without a model call: a confined process cannot read the host Codex login or OpenCode
database, sees no credential-named environment variable, and cannot read the held-out copy in either
checkout. The OpenCode copy holds 0 of 18 provider values after forgetting (2 of 18 before). Verified
live, one Codex run (control arm, `openai/gpt-6-luna`): the agent's own shell reported both host
stores denied and a credential-variable count of 0; its 5 login values were in 0 kept files and 0
events; its login copy was removed after the run. Not verified live: OpenCode. Its provider returned
HTTP 400 on the pinned OpenAI credential before any tool call (`provider.auth`), as Amendment 2
recorded, so there is no OpenCode tool run to inspect.

Accepted residuals: an agent can read its own login copy and has network access, so it could send
its own login out; a network allowlist to the model host would close this and is not implemented.
The hidden list is a denylist: the rest of the host is readable read-only, so an answer stored
outside the listed paths would be readable to an agent.

Amendment 5, before any held-out look (review of PR #52): (1) every `git` command on the agent's
tree, including `git apply` of the hidden test patch and the editable install's build hooks, runs
under the same bubblewrap confinement; a planted clean filter no longer runs on the host (tests
in `tests/python/test_agent_run.py` and `test_agent_environment.py`). (2) `/run` and `/var/run`
are masked so host sockets (docker, systemd) are unreachable; name-service files are re-bound.
(3) Run artifacts are written with `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW` after unlinking, and a symlinked OpenCode
credential database is removed, never opened. (4) On the agent's tree only a failed bubblewrap
launch is a harness error; a hang, a broken `conftest.py` or a collection error is the agent's
unresolved result (gold-patch verification stays strict). (5) `report` prints `provisional` unless the
adjacent manifest's whole task x arm x
repetition matrix is scored, or when the manifest is missing. Residuals: the agent and build hooks
keep network access, the hidden-test pytest runs the agent's own `conftest.py` (it could forge
`PASSED` lines), test files are restored from the agent-writable `.git`, and sockets outside
`/run` (for example abstract or `/tmp/.X11-unix`) are not filtered.

## Commands

Before a held-out run, generate and verify its local task set with
`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py`; this writes
`fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json` and a rejection log. The generator requires
GitHub CLI access and builds candidate repositories; its selection rule is in `heldout.py`.

See the docstring of `scripts/agent_eval/__main__.py`. Verdicts are one row in
[`docs/decisions.md`](../../../docs/decisions.md).

"""Executable task set: SWE-bench Verified instances whose tests run here.

``fetch`` narrows the pinned dataset to the repositories this harness can build.
``verify`` keeps an instance only when, in a fresh environment built from its base commit,
the dataset's fail-to-pass tests fail before the gold patch and pass after it. Its pass-to-pass
set is cut to the tests that pass both before and after, so an environment gap cannot
count against an arm.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import importlib
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
import threading
from collections.abc import Callable
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import confine

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
# Dev: the dataset-pinned tasks every run to date has used (spent, not held-out).
TASKS = ROOT / "fixtures" / "eval" / "agent-swe" / "tasks.json"
# Held-out: built from PRs merged after a cutoff, opened once per set (see heldout.py).
HELDOUT = ROOT / "fixtures" / "eval" / "agent-swe" / "heldout-tasks.json"
CACHE = Path(os.environ.get("OXIDE_EVAL_CACHE", Path.home() / ".cache" / "oxide" / "agent-eval"))
MIRRORS = Path.home() / ".cache" / "oxide" / "contextbench" / "git"  # bare, from contextbench.py
DATASET = "princeton-nlp/SWE-bench_Verified@c104f840cc67f8b6eec6f759ebc8b2693d585d4a"
# Pure-Python repositories whose tests are pytest node ids; Python as SWE-bench builds them.
REPOS = {
    "pytest-dev/pytest": ("3.9", "testing"),
    "psf/requests": ("3.9", None),
    "pallets/flask": ("3.9", None),
    "pylint-dev/pylint": ("3.9", None),
    "mwaskom/seaborn": ("3.9", None),
}
RESULT = re.compile(r"^(PASSED|FAILED|ERROR|SKIPPED|XFAIL|XPASS) (\S.*?)(?: - .*)?$")


def path_for(split: str) -> Path:
    if split not in {"dev", "heldout"}:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown split {split!r}")
    return TASKS if split == "dev" else HELDOUT


def load(split: str = "dev") -> list[dict[str, Any]]:
    path = path_for(split)
    if split == "heldout" and not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(
            "held-out tasks are not in the checkout; generate and verify them with "
            "`uv run python scripts/agent_eval/heldout.py` "
            "(writes fixtures/eval/agent-swe/heldout-tasks.json) before "
            "`run --split heldout --final`"
        )
    tasks: list[dict[str, Any]] = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["tasks"]
    return tasks


def order(task: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The predeclared, seed-free task order for ``run --tasks N``."""
    return hashlib.sha256(task["id"].encode()).hexdigest()


def sh(
    *argv: str | Path,
    cwd: Path | None = None,
    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,
    timeout: int = 900,
) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess[str]:
    return subprocess.run(
        [str(a) for a in argv],
        cwd=cwd,
        env={**confine.clean_env({}), **(env or {})},
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        timeout=timeout,
        check=False,
    )


def fetch(parquet: Path, out: Path) -> None:
    """Candidate rows of ``REPOS`` from the dataset's parquet (needs ``--with pyarrow``)."""
    rows = importlib.import_module("pyarrow.parquet").read_table(parquet).to_pylist()
    keep = [r for r in rows if r["repo"] in REPOS]
    out.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    out.write_text(json.dumps(keep), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"{len(keep)} candidates of {len(rows)} rows -> {out}")


_CLONE = threading.Lock()


def _mirror(repo: str, commit: str) -> Path:
    """A bare repository holding ``commit``: the contextbench mirror if it has it, else a
    full clone of its own, made once."""
…
    return CACHE / "git" / name

"""Confinement for everything that runs on an agent's tree: the agent itself, and the hidden-test
pytest that runs on its output afterwards.

The agent edits files the harness later executes (``conftest.py``, test files, ``.git/config``),
so those processes are as untrusted as the agent. Each runs under bubblewrap: the host read-only,
the answers and other runs hidden, and one writable directory. Confinement is fail-closed: with
no bubblewrap, no run starts.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

# The only host variables a confined process inherits. Credentials are not among them: the
# agent's own login is a copy inside its run directory, and every other key stays on the host.
KEEP_ENV = (
    "PATH",
    "HOME",
    "USER",
    "LOGNAME",
    "SHELL",
    "LANG",
    "LC_ALL",
    "LC_CTYPE",
    "TERM",
    "TZ",
    "SSL_CERT_FILE",
    "SSL_CERT_DIR",
    "HTTP_PROXY",
    "HTTPS_PROXY",
    "NO_PROXY",
    "http_proxy",
    "https_proxy",
    "no_proxy",
    "UV_CACHE_DIR",
    "UV_PYTHON_INSTALL_DIR",
)

# Home-relative credential stores, hidden whole from every confined process.
SECRET_PATHS = (
    ".codex",
    ".claude",
    ".omp",
    ".pi",
    ".ssh",
    ".gnupg",
    ".aws",
    ".config",
    ".netrc",
    ".git-credentials",
    ".npmrc",
    ".pypirc",
    ".local/share/opencode",
    ".claude.json",
    ".cursor",
    ".copilot",
    ".gemini",
    ".cline",
    ".docker",
    ".kube",
    ".modal.toml",
    ".bash_history",
    ".zsh_history",
)

# A read-only bind still allows connect() to Unix sockets. These dirs hold the host's.
_RUNTIME = (Path("/run"), Path("/var/run"))
# libc reads these; they are often symlinks into the runtime dirs above.
_NAME_SERVICE = (Path("/etc/resolv.conf"), Path("/etc/hosts"))
_MASK_FAILED = (
    "bubblewrap confinement cannot mask host runtime sockets without breaking name resolution"
)


def runtime_dirs(candidates: Iterable[Path] = _RUNTIME) -> list[Path]:
    """Real runtime directories to replace. A symlink is not a mount point: bubblewrap
    refuses ``--tmpfs`` on one, and the directory it points at is already covered."""
    chosen: list[Path] = []
    seen: set[Path] = set()
    for path in candidates:

            real = path.resolve()
        except OSError as exc:
            raise SystemExit(_MASK_FAILED) from exc
        if real in seen or not real.is_dir():
            continue
        seen.add(real)
        chosen.append(real if path.is_symlink() else path)
    return chosen

In an OpenCode run, the agent can rename `base/data/opencode` and replace it with a symlink to the host's `~/.local/share/opencode`. The leaf `opencode.db` is then a regular file, so `db.is_symlink()` returns false. After confinement ends, this unconfined SQLite connection follows the parent symlink and executes `DELETE FROM credential` and `VACUUM` against the host's real database, erasing its provider credentials despite the sandbox's read-only mount. Confine credential cleanup too, or use trusted directory descriptors and no-follow traversal for every path component.

That meant fixing the valid review findings and the failing CI. All the fixes are done and `mise run verify` passes.█- **Latest request: "Commit on that PR branch".** The fixed files are not yet committed.█## Constraints & Preferences█- Repo rules: follow `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.█- Every OXIDE source file must be ≤500 LOC; tests and docs are exempt.█- The gate is `mise run verify` (ruff, mypy --strict, pytest).█- The frozen baseline `fixtures/eval/structural-v1/` is a read-only oracle and must never be edited.█- AGENTS.md: commit on the current worktree branch after `mise run verify` passes, without asking. Don't push, tag or release unless asked.█- Bash policy blocks `grep`, `rg`, `cat`, `head` and `tail` as commands; use the `grep` and `read` tools. Never use sed, perl or python for individual edits; use `edit` (hashline `[path#TAG]`). A retry after the "never displayed" notice works.█- Ponytail mode is active: smallest complete change, and end the final reply with 1-2 lines on what was skipped or the risk.█- Before declaring complete, verify consistency (all call sites), scope (minimal diff) and verification (full module run).█## Progress█### Done█- [x] Fixed the CI failures: 5 tests failed with `SystemExit: bubblewrap (bwrap) is required` on the Windows, macOS and Linux platform jobs.█- The runner tests now stub `confine.require` / `confine.confine`. The files are `test_agent_cap.py`, `test_agent_codex.py` and `test_agent_confine.py`.█- A run with `shutil.which` patched to hide bwrap gave 67 passed, 8 skipped. The Windows and macOS jobs themselves have not been seen.█- [x] Review findings fixed:█- Confined git add/diff/checkout/cat-file, `git apply` (new `wrap=`/`scratch=` parameters on `tasks.apply`), the confined `rm`, and the editable-install build hooks.█- Masked `/run` and `/var/run`; extended `SECRET_PATHS` (`.claude.json`, `.cursor`, `.copilot`, `.gemini`, `.cline`, `.docker`, `.kube`, `.modal.toml`, `.bash_history`, `.zsh_history`).█- `write_private` uses `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`.█- `forget_credentials` unlinks a symlinked DB instead of opening it.█- Credential cleanup now runs on early failures: the login copy in `codex.py` is moved just before the guarded `try`, and `agent()` in `run.py` wraps all steps in `try/finally`.█- Spend is recorded before the trace write.█- Nested JSON credentials are extracted for redaction.█- `report.plan_block` gives `provisional` for an incomplete matrix or a missing manifest. The test was flipped to `test_results_without_a_manifest_are_not_a_final_verdict`.█- `tasks.tests(agent_tree=True)` makes a hang, a broken conftest or a collection error an unresolved result. Only a bwrap launch failure raises `TestRunError`. Gold verification stays strict.█- `score()` passes `agent_tree=True`.█- `arms.base_import_root` is now lenient. New `arms.check_base_src` raises SystemExit and is called from `run_all`. This fixed a HIGH bug the code review found: `batch.manifest` crashed on the `oxide-base` placeholder. A new test `test_the_manifest_builds_for_every_arm_without_a_base_snapshot` covers it.█- `run.py` is split into 359 lines, with `arms`, `events`, `session`, `codex` and `batch` modules. Every source file is ≤359 lines.█- Added the spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-agent-eval-harness-design.md`, to satisfy the Tier 2 review gate's "intent spec" requirement.█- Added "Amendment 5" and the held-out generation note to `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`.█- New tests: the real-bwrap `git apply` clean-filter escape test (with an unconfined control), the `agent_tree` scoring tests, and the manifest test.█- [x] Final verification:█- `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `mypy --strict scripts/agent_eval` are clean.█- `pytest tests/python/test_agent_*.py` gave 75 passed.█- `mise run verify` gave 549 passed, 7 skipped.█- [x] All 9 todo items are marked done.█- [x] Independent SecReview and CodeReview agents have finished. They are idle.█### In Progress█- [ ] **Commit onto `feat/secure-agent-eval-harness`.**█- I just ran `git fetch origin feat/secure-agent-eval-harness`. FETCH_HEAD is `5a75ff7` ("Merge branch 'main' into feat/secure-agent-eval-harness"), which sits on top of `27d4a1b` ("feat(eval): confine agent runs; isolate Codex and OpenCode credentials") and `33d4ae1`.█- `git diff --stat main FETCH_HEAD` shows 21 files, +5316/-2.█- A local branch `feat/secure-agent-eval-harness` already exists (`git branch -a` marks it with `+`, which means it is checked out in another worktree).█- The current checkout is `main` at `f26e37e` ("Enable Entire"), ahead of origin/main by 2.█- `git status --short` shows these untracked on `main`:█- `scripts/agent_eval/`, `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/`, `tests/python/test_agent_{cap,codex,confine,diagnose,environment,eval,protocol,report,run}.py`█- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-agent-eval-harness-design.md`█- Not mine: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-07-oxide-search-discoverability-design.md`, `.omp/`, `.pi/tasks/`█### Blocked█- None. That meant fixing the valid review findings and the failing CI. All the fixes are done and `mise run verify` passes.█- **Latest request: "Commit on that PR branch".** The fixed files are not yet committed.█## Constraints & Preferences█- Repo rules: follow `AGENTS.md` and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`.█- Every OXIDE source file must be ≤500 LOC; tests and docs are exempt.█- The gate is `mise run verify` (ruff, mypy --strict, pytest).█- The frozen baseline `fixtures/eval/structural-v1/` is a read-only oracle and must never be edited.█- AGENTS.md: commit on the current worktree branch after `mise run verify` passes, without asking. Don't push, tag or release unless asked.█- Bash policy blocks `grep`, `rg`, `cat`, `head` and `tail` as commands; use the `grep` and `read` tools. Never use sed, perl or python for individual edits; use `edit` (hashline `[path#TAG]`). A retry after the "never displayed" notice works.█- Ponytail mode is active: smallest complete change, and end the final reply with 1-2 lines on what was skipped or the risk.█- Before declaring complete, verify consistency (all call sites), scope (minimal diff) and verification (full module run).█## Progress█### Done█- [x] Fixed the CI failures: 5 tests failed with `SystemExit: bubblewrap (bwrap) is required` on the Windows, macOS and Linux platform jobs.█- The runner tests now stub `confine.require` / `confine.confine`. The files are `test_agent_cap.py`, `test_agent_codex.py` and `test_agent_confine.py`.█- A run with `shutil.which` patched to hide bwrap gave 67 passed, 8 skipped. The Windows and macOS jobs themselves have not been seen.█- [x] Review findings fixed:█- Confined git add/diff/checkout/cat-file, `git apply` (new `wrap=`/`scratch=` parameters on `tasks.apply`), the confined `rm`, and the editable-install build hooks.█- Masked `/run` and `/var/run`; extended `SECRET_PATHS` (`.claude.json`, `.cursor`, `.copilot`, `.gemini`, `.cline`, `.docker`, `.kube`, `.modal.toml`, `.bash_history`, `.zsh_history`).█- `write_private` uses `O_EXCL | O_NOFOLLOW`.█- `forget_credentials` unlinks a symlinked DB instead of opening it.█- Credential cleanup now runs on early failures: the login copy in `codex.py` is moved just before the guarded `try`, and `agent()` in `run.py` wraps all steps in `try/finally`.█- Spend is recorded before the trace write.█- Nested JSON credentials are extracted for redaction.█- `report.plan_block` gives `provisional` for an incomplete matrix or a missing manifest. The test was flipped to `test_results_without_a_manifest_are_not_a_final_verdict`.█- `tasks.tests(agent_tree=True)` makes a hang, a broken conftest or a collection error an unresolved result. Only a bwrap launch failure raises `TestRunError`. Gold verification stays strict.█- `score()` passes `agent_tree=True`.█- `arms.base_import_root` is now lenient. New `arms.check_base_src` raises SystemExit and is called from `run_all`. This fixed a HIGH bug the code review found: `batch.manifest` crashed on the `oxide-base` placeholder. A new test `test_the_manifest_builds_for_every_arm_without_a_base_snapshot` covers it.█- `run.py` is split into 359 lines, with `arms`, `events`, `session`, `codex` and `batch` modules. Every source file is ≤359 lines.█- Added the spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-08-agent-eval-harness-design.md`, to satisfy the Tier 2 review gate's "intent spec" requirement.█- Added "Amendment 5" and the held-out generation note to `fixtures/eval/agent-swe/README.md`.█- New tests: the real-bwrap `git apply` clean-filter escape test (with an unconfined control), the `agent_tree` scoring tests, and the manifest test.█- [x] Final verification:█- `ruff format`, `ruff check` and `mypy --strict scripts/agent_eval` are clean.█- `pytest tests/python/test_agent_*.py` gave 75 passed.█- `mise run verify` gave 549 passed, 7 skipped.█- [x] All 9 todo items are marked done.█- [x] Independent SecReview and CodeReview agents have finished. def launch(
…
    """Runs one agent CLI to completion or timeout; a timeout kills its whole process group."""
    process = subprocess.Popen(
        command,
        cwd=cwd,
        env=environment,
        stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL,
        stdout=subprocess.PIPE,
        stderr=subprocess.STDOUT,
        text=True,
        encoding="utf-8",
        errors="replace",
        start_new_session=True,
    )
    _launch_state.started = True
    _launch_state.raw = ""
    try:
        out, _ = process.communicate(timeout=timeout)
        _launch_state.raw = out or ""
        return ("ok" if process.returncode == 0 else f"exit {process.returncode}"), out
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired as error:
        if isinstance(error.output, bytes):
            _launch_state.raw = error.output.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
        else:
            _launch_state.raw = error.output or ""
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        out, _ = process.communicate()
        _launch_state.raw = out or ""
        return "timeout", out or ""


def run_one(
    task: dict[str, Any], arm: str, rep: int, args: argparse.Namespace, root: Path
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    key = f"{task['id']}.{arm}.{rep}"
    base = root / key
    work, data = base / "work", base / "oxide-data"
    using_codex = args.runner == "codex"
    row: dict[str, Any] = {
        "task": task["id"],
        "arm": arm,
        "rep": rep,
        "model": args.model,
        "split": args.split,
        "runner": args.runner,
    }
    _launch_state.started = False
    _launch_state.raw = ""
    row["usage_unknown"] = False
    try:
        tasks.checkout(task, work)
        env = tasks.environment(task, work, base / "venv")
        if not using_codex:
            home = base / "config" / "opencode"
            home.mkdir(parents=True)
            cfg = arms.config(arm, work, data, args.base_src)
            (home / "opencode.jsonc").write_text(json.dumps(cfg), encoding="utf-8")
        if arm in arms.OXIDE_ARMS:  # cost of indexing is reported separately
            started = time.monotonic()
            indexed = tasks.sh(
                *arms.oxide_command(arm, args.base_src, "index", work, "--data-dir", data),
                env={"OXIDE_DATA_DIR": str(data)},
            )
            row["index_seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 2)
            if indexed.returncode:
                raise RuntimeError(f"oxide index: {indexed.stderr[-300:]}")
        if using_codex:
            started = time.monotonic()
            command = arms.mcp_command(arm, work, data, args.base_src)
            row["status"], raw = codex.codex_agent(
                args.model, arm, task, base, env, args.timeout, command
            )
        else:
            credentials(args.model, base / "data")
            started = time.monotonic()
            row["status"], raw = agent(args.model, arm, task, base, env, args.timeout)
        row["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 1)
        # before any trace write or failure below: a failed run still spent tokens
        row |= (codex.codex_measure if using_codex else events.measure)(raw)
        reason = codex.codex_agent_error if using_codex else events.agent_error
        row["usage_unknown"] = (
            row["status"] != "ok"
            or not row.pop("usage_complete", False)
            or bool(reason(raw))
        )
        row["spend"] = protocol.spend(row["tokens"])
        session.write_private(base / "events.jsonl", raw)
        row["events_sha256"] = protocol.sha256_bytes(raw.encode())
        row["oxide_tools_connected"] = (
            codex.codex_connected(arm) if using_codex else session.connected(base / "data", arm)
        )
        reason = codex.codex_agent_error if using_codex else events.agent_error
        if failure := events.agent_failure(row["status"], raw, reason):
            raise RuntimeError(failure)
        if using_codex:
            codex.codex_isolation(arm, raw)
        else:
            session.isolation(arm, base)
        session.git_on_agent(base, "add", "-A", cwd=work)
        diff = session.git_on_agent(
            base,
            "diff",
            "--cached",
            "--no-ext-diff",
            "--no-textconv",
            "HEAD",
            "--",
            ".",
            ":!*.egg-info",
            cwd=work,
        )
        session.write_private(base / "patch.diff", diff.stdout)
        row |= session.score(task, work, env, base)
    except (RuntimeError, subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError, sqlite3.Error) as error:
        if _launch_state.started and "spend" not in row:
            raw = _launch_state.raw
            row |= (codex.codex_measure if using_codex else events.measure)(raw)
            row.pop("usage_complete", None)
            row["spend"] = protocol.spend(row["tokens"])
        if _launch_state.started:
            row["usage_unknown"] = True
        row |= {"status": "harness-error", "error": str(error)[-400:], "resolved": None}
    row["trace"] = str(base.relative_to(tasks.CACHE))  # events, patch, data: kept, never pruned
    shutil.rmtree(work, ignore_errors=True)
    shutil.rmtree(base / "venv", ignore_errors=True)
    return row

def run_all(args: argparse.Namespace) -> None:
    confine.require()
…

    def work(job: tuple[dict[str, Any], str, int]) -> None:
        nonlocal largest
        with ready:  # a run starts only if the cap still holds with every run in flight
            if cap is not None and state["unknown"]:
                state["skipped"] += 1
                return
            while not protocol.admit(state["spent"], state["in_flight"], largest, cap):
                if state["in_flight"] == 0:  # nothing running can free budget: the cap is spent
                    state["skipped"] += 1
                    return
                ready.wait()  # an in-flight run reports its spend; then the check repeats
                if cap is not None and state["unknown"]:
                    state["skipped"] += 1
                    return
            state["in_flight"] += 1
        try:
            row = run_one(*job, args, root)
        except BaseException:
            with ready:
                state["in_flight"] -= 1
                ready.notify_all()
            raise
        with ready, out.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as file:
            file.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")
            state["in_flight"] -= 1  # same lock as the spend: the cap is never blind
            if "spend" in row:
                state["spent"] += row["spend"]
                largest = max(largest or 0, row["spend"])
            state["unknown"] = state["unknown"] or row.get("usage_unknown", False)
            ready.notify_all()
        print(
            f"{row['task']} {row['arm']}#{row['rep']}: {row['status']} resolved={row['resolved']}"
            f" spend={row.get('spend', 0)}",
            flush=True,
        )

    with ThreadPoolExecutor(args.jobs) as executor:
        list(executor.map(work, jobs))
    print(f"{len(jobs) - state['skipped']} of {len(jobs)} runs -> {out}; {state['spent']} tokens")
    if state["skipped"]:
        print(f"token cap {args.max_tokens} reached: {state['skipped']} runs not started")

"""Codex exec: isolated login, arm config, and the JSON stream it prints."""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import os
import shutil
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import arms
import confine
import events

# Codex runs use the ChatGPT login in CODEX_HOME/auth.json, copied into each run's isolated home.
CODEX = Path(shutil.which("codex") or "codex")
CODEX_AUTH = Path.home() / ".codex" / "auth.json"


def codex_config(command: list[str], fts: Path) -> str:
    """Codex config for one arm: the OXIDE server alone, or no server for control. JSON strings
    are valid TOML basic strings for these paths, so the arrays are written as JSON."""
    if not command:
        return ""
    return (
        "[mcp_servers.oxide]\n"
        f"command = {json.dumps(command[0])}\n"
        f"args = {json.dumps(command[1:])}\n"
        f"env = {{ OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION = {json.dumps(str(fts))} }}\n"
    )


def codex_model(model: str) -> str:
    """Codex takes the bare model id under a ChatGPT login; only the openai provider is routed
    through it, so any other provider is refused rather than silently remapped."""
    provider, _, name = model.partition("/")
    if provider != "openai" or not name:
        raise SystemExit(f"--runner codex needs an openai/<model> id, got {model!r}")
    return name


def codex_agent(
    model: str,
    arm: str,
    task: dict[str, Any],
    base: Path,
    env: dict[str, str],
    timeout: int,
    command: list[str],
) -> tuple[str, str]:
    """Runs ``codex exec`` with an isolated home: the ChatGPT login and this arm's MCP server only.
    User config, user MCP servers and user instructions are not read."""
    import run

    work, home = base / "work", base / "codex"
    prompt = arms.PROMPT.format(hint=arms.HINT[arm], problem=task["problem"].strip())
    home.mkdir(parents=True)
    (home / "config.toml").write_text(codex_config(command, run.fts_location()), encoding="utf-8")
    environment = confine.clean_env(
        {
            **env,
            "CODEX_HOME": str(home),
            "HOME": str(base / "home"),
            "OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION": str(run.fts_location()),
        }
    )
    argv = [
        str(CODEX),
        "exec",
        "--json",
        "--ephemeral",
        "--skip-git-repo-check",
        "-m",
        codex_model(model),
        "-s",
        "workspace-write",
        "-C",
        str(work),
        prompt,
    ]
    if not CODEX_AUTH.exists():
        raise SystemExit(f"no codex login at {CODEX_AUTH}: run `codex login`")
    secrets = confine.json_secrets(CODEX_AUTH)  # the login's values, redacted from kept events
    directory = os.open(home, os.O_RDONLY | os.O_DIRECTORY | os.O_NOFOLLOW)
    fd = None
    try:
        shutil.copy2(CODEX_AUTH, home / "auth.json")
        fd = os.open("auth.json", os.O_RDWR | os.O_NOFOLLOW, dir_fd=directory)
        os.fchmod(fd, 0o600)
        wrapped = confine.confine(argv, writable=base, hide=run.hidden(), net=True)
        status, raw = run.launch(wrapped, work, environment, timeout)
    finally:
        try:
            try:
                if fd is not None:
                    os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
            finally:
                try:
                    os.unlink("auth.json", dir_fd=directory)
                except FileNotFoundError:
                    pass
        finally:
            if fd is not None:
                os.close(fd)
            os.close(directory)
    return status, confine.redact(raw, secrets)


def codex_measure(raw: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Tokens, steps and tool calls from ``codex exec --json``. Codex counts cached input inside
    input_tokens, so the uncached share is recorded as input and cache_read is not billed twice.
    Output tokens already include reasoning."""
    tokens = {"input": 0, "output": 0, "cache_read": 0, "cache_write": 0}
    calls: dict[str, int] = {}
    steps = 0
    complete = False
    for event in events._jsonl(raw):
        if event.get("type") in {"turn.started", "turn.failed"}:
            complete = False
        if event.get("type") == "item.completed":
            item = event.get("item", {})
            kind = item.get("type")
            if kind in {"agent_message", "reasoning", "error"}:
                continue
            name = item.get("tool") if kind == "mcp_tool_call" else kind
            calls[str(name)] = calls.get(str(name), 0) + 1
        elif event.get("type") == "turn.completed":
            steps += 1
            used = event.get("usage")
            if not isinstance(used, dict):
                used = {}
            complete = all(
                isinstance(used.get(key), int) and used[key] >= 0
                for key in ("input_tokens", "output_tokens")
            )
            total = used.get("input_tokens", 0)
            cached = used.get("cached_input_tokens", 0)
            output = used.get("output_tokens", 0)
            if not isinstance(total, int) or total < 0:
                total = 0
            if not isinstance(cached, int) or not 0 <= cached <= total:
                complete = False
                cached = 0
            if not isinstance(output, int) or output < 0:
                output = 0
            tokens["input"] += total - cached
            tokens["cache_read"] += cached
            tokens["output"] += output
    return {
        "tokens": tokens,
        "steps": steps,
        "calls": calls,
        "usage_complete": complete and not events.incomplete_json(raw),
    }


def codex_agent_error(raw: str) -> str | None:
    """A failed turn, or an error with no completed turn. An error inside a turn that then
    completed is a retry, not a failure."""
    stream = events._jsonl(raw)
    failed = [
        e.get("error", {}).get("message", "turn failed")
        for e in stream
        if e.get("type") == "turn.failed"
    ]
    if failed:
        return str(failed[-1])
    if any(e.get("type") == "turn.completed" for e in stream):
        return None
    errors = [str(e.get("message", "agent error")) for e in stream if e.get("type") == "error"]
    return errors[-1] if errors else None


def codex_isolation(arm: str, raw: str) -> None:
    """Reject runs whose MCP tool calls came from a server other than the arm's own."""
    servers = {
        str(e["item"].get("server"))
        for e in events._jsonl(raw)
        if e.get("type") == "item.completed" and e.get("item", {}).get("type") == "mcp_tool_call"
    }
    if not servers <= ({"oxide"} if arm in arms.OXIDE_ARMS else set()):
        raise RuntimeError(f"isolation: unexpected MCP servers {sorted(servers)}")


def codex_connected(arm: str) -> int:
    """OXIDE tools configured for this arm. Codex's JSON stream does not log MCP startup, so this
    is the configured count, not an observed one; the calls themselves are observed in events."""
    return 1 if arm in arms.OXIDE_ARMS else 0

"""The Codex runner's parsers, on event lines captured from ``codex exec --json`` (codex-cli
0.165.0). No model is called: this checks how the harness reads a run, not the agent."""

from __future__ import annotations

import importlib
import json
import sys
import tomllib
from pathlib import Path
from types import ModuleType

import pytest

SCRIPTS = str(Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2] / "scripts" / "agent_eval")
if SCRIPTS not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, SCRIPTS)

codex: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("codex")
protocol: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("protocol")
run: ModuleType = importlib.import_module("run")

FTS = Path("/cache/libfts.lbug_extension")

MCP_ITEM = {
    "id": "item_1",
    "type": "mcp_tool_call",
    "server": "oxide",
    "tool": "oxide_search",
    "arguments": {"query": "parse_budget", "mode": "search"},
    "result": {"content": [{"type": "text", "text": '{"entries_returned": 1}'}]},
    "error": None,
    "status": "completed",
}

OK_RUN = "\n".join(
    json.dumps(event)
    for event in (
        {"type": "thread.started", "thread_id": "t"},
        {"type": "turn.started"},
        {"type": "item.completed", "item": MCP_ITEM},
        {
            "type": "item.completed",
            "item": {"id": "item_2", "type": "agent_message", "text": "cfg.py"},
        },
        {
            "type": "turn.completed",
            "usage": {
                "input_tokens": 44326,
                "cached_input_tokens": 39936,
                "cache_write_input_tokens": 0,
                "output_tokens": 100,
                "reasoning_output_tokens": 0,
            },
        },
    )
)

MODEL_REFUSED = "\n".join(
    json.dumps(event)
    for event in (
        {"type": "thread.started", "thread_id": "t"},
        {"type": "turn.started"},
        {"type": "error", "message": "The 'no-such-model-xyz' model is not supported."},
        {
            "type": "turn.failed",
            "error": {"message": "The 'no-such-model-xyz' model is not supported."},
        },
    )
)


def test_cached_input_is_billed_once_and_the_spend_equals_the_reported_tokens() -> None:
    measured = codex.codex_measure(OK_RUN)
    assert measured["tokens"] == {
        "input": 44326 - 39936,
        "output": 100,
        "cache_read": 39936,
        "cache_write": 0,
    }
    assert protocol.spend(measured["tokens"]) == 44326 + 100


def test_only_completed_items_count_as_calls_and_messages_do_not() -> None:
    measured = codex.codex_measure(OK_RUN)
    assert measured["calls"] == {"oxide_search": 1}
    assert measured["steps"] == 1


def test_a_failed_turn_is_reported_as_the_agent_failure() -> None:
    assert codex.codex_agent_error(MODEL_REFUSED) == (
        "The 'no-such-model-xyz' model is not supported."
    )


def test_an_error_inside_a_turn_that_completes_is_not_a_failure() -> None:
    retried = OK_RUN.replace(
        '{"type": "turn.started"}',
        '{"type": "turn.started"}\n{"type": "error", "message": "reconnecting"}',
    )
    assert codex.codex_agent_error(retried) is None


def test_usage_completeness_requires_terminal_usage() -> None:
    assert codex.codex_measure(OK_RUN)["usage_complete"] is True
    assert codex.codex_measure('{"type":"thread.started"}')["usage_complete"] is False
    assert codex.codex_measure('{"type":"turn.completed"}')["usage_complete"] is False
    assert codex.codex_measure(OK_RUN + '\n{"type":"turn.failed"}')["usage_complete"] is False


def test_the_arm_config_names_only_the_oxide_server_and_control_names_none() -> None:
    command = ["/venv/bin/python", "-m", "oxide", "mcp", "--repo", "/w", "--data-dir", "/d"]
    parsed = tomllib.loads(codex.codex_config(command, FTS))
    assert parsed == {
        "mcp_servers": {
            "oxide": {
                "command": "/venv/bin/python",
                "args": ["-m", "oxide", "mcp", "--repo", "/w", "--data-dir", "/d"],
                "env": {"OXIDE_FTS_EXTENSION": str(FTS)},
            }
        }
    }
    assert codex.codex_config([], FTS) == ""


def test_a_tool_call_from_another_server_fails_isolation() -> None:
    foreign = OK_RUN.replace('"server": "oxide"', '"server": "github"')
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="isolation"):
        codex.codex_isolation("oxide", foreign)
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="isolation"):
        codex.codex_isolation("control", OK_RUN)
    codex.codex_isolation("oxide", OK_RUN)


def test_codex_takes_the_bare_openai_model_id_and_refuses_other_providers() -> None:
    assert codex.codex_model("openai/gpt-6-luna") == "gpt-6-luna"
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="openai"):
        codex.codex_model("opencode/gpt-6-luna")
    with pytest.raises(SystemExit, match="openai"):
        codex.codex_model("gpt-6-luna")


def test_the_copied_login_is_removed_after_the_run_even_when_it_fails(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    login = tmp_path / "auth.json"
    login.write_text('{"token": "not-a-real-login"}', encoding="utf-8")
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex, "CODEX_AUTH", login)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "fts_location", lambda: FTS)
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex.confine, "confine", lambda argv, **_: list(argv))

    def launch_fails(*_: object) -> tuple[str, str]:
        raise RuntimeError("launch failed")

    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "launch", launch_fails)
    base = tmp_path / "run"
    with pytest.raises(RuntimeError, match="launch failed"):
        codex.codex_agent("openai/gpt-6-luna", "oxide", {"problem": "p"}, base, {}, 1, [])
    assert not (base / "codex" / "auth.json").exists()
    assert (base / "codex" / "config.toml").exists()


@pytest.mark.skipif(sys.platform == "win32", reason="requires symlinks")
def test_codex_cleanup_pins_login_when_parent_is_replaced(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    login = tmp_path / "login.json"
    login.write_text('{"token": "secret-value"}', encoding="utf-8")
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex, "CODEX_AUTH", login)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "fts_location", lambda: FTS)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "hidden", lambda: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex.confine, "confine", lambda argv, **_: argv)
    base = tmp_path / "run"
    moved = base / "moved"
    victim = tmp_path / "victim"
    victim.mkdir()
    (victim / "auth.json").write_text("untouched", encoding="utf-8")

    def launch(*_: object) -> tuple[str, str]:
        (base / "codex").rename(moved)
        (base / "codex").symlink_to(victim, target_is_directory=True)
        return "ok", ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "launch", launch)
    codex.codex_agent("openai/model", "control", {"problem": "p"}, base, {}, 1, [])
    assert (victim / "auth.json").read_text() == "untouched"
    assert not (moved / "auth.json").exists()


def test_codex_cleanup_does_not_truncate_replacement_hardlink(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    login = tmp_path / "login.json"
    login.write_text('{"token": "secret-value"}', encoding="utf-8")
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex, "CODEX_AUTH", login)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "fts_location", lambda: FTS)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "hidden", lambda: [])
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex.confine, "confine", lambda argv, **_: argv)
    base = tmp_path / "run"
    victim = tmp_path / "victim"
    victim.write_text("untouched", encoding="utf-8")
    moved = base / "codex" / "moved.json"

    def launch(*_: object) -> tuple[str, str]:
        auth = base / "codex" / "auth.json"
        auth.rename(moved)
        auth.hardlink_to(victim)
        return "ok", ""

    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "launch", launch)
    codex.codex_agent("openai/model", "control", {"problem": "p"}, base, {}, 1, [])
    assert victim.read_text() == "untouched"
    assert b"secret-value" not in moved.read_bytes()


def test_codex_removes_partial_login_on_copy_failure(
    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch
) -> None:
    login = tmp_path / "login.json"
    login.write_text('{"token": "secret-value"}', encoding="utf-8")
    monkeypatch.setattr(codex, "CODEX_AUTH", login)
    monkeypatch.setattr(run, "fts_location", lambda: FTS)

    def copy_fails(source: object, destination: object) -> None:
        Path(destination).write_text("secret-value", encoding="utf-8")
        raise OSError("copy failed")

    monkeypatch.setattr(codex.shutil, "copy2", copy_fails)
    base = tmp_path / "run"
    with pytest.raises(OSError, match="copy failed"):
        codex.codex_agent("openai/model", "control", {"problem": "p"}, base, {}, 1, [])
    assert not (base / "codex" / "auth.json").exists()
